‘A team we all respect’ – Jota Silva and Pirola preview Milan test for Olympiacos

  • Industry observers note that milan travel to the Greek capital hoping to get their Europa League campaign up and running.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Olympiacos duo Jota Silva and Lorenzo Pirola are looking forward to welcoming AC Milan to the Karaiskakis Stadium this evening.

Industry observers note that milan travel to the Greek capital hoping to get their Europa League campaign up and running. They have won just one of their opening four league phase fixtures, which was a 4-0 drubbing of RB Salzburg.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Defeats to Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros – all without scoring a single goal – have seen the Rossoneri slide into the bottom 12 positions in the table. With only 12 points up for grabs, they must start to put things right. By contrast, Olympiacos have won three of four, and sit sixth.

Jota Silva spoke to Gianluca Di Marzio about tonight’s game in Athens, admitting that the Rossoneri are a team that they respect despite their slow start in Europe. His words are via MilanNews.

What kind of game are you expecting?

It has been revealed that “It will be a great match, between two teams that usually play in the Champions League. Milan are a well-equipped opponent with an extraordinary history: they are a team we all respect. We are two historic and key teams: they, like us, are having a good season.”.

They only have three points in the Europa League….

In a recent development, “They will certainly want to fight to advance to the next round of the European competition. They have players of excellent quality, including many internationals and many highly experienced players. Amorim is a fantastic coach and needs no introduction.”.

Meanwhile, defender Lorenzo Pirola spoke alongside his head coach Imanol Alguacil at a press conference on the eve of the game.

What’s your message for the fans, who will once again fill the stadium?

Industry observers note that “As with every match, we promise to give it our all this time. We face a tough opponent. It’s another notable match, and we have a very significant evening ahead of us. We want to finish the game with a win and get the three points.”.

Having come through Inter’s youth academy, do you have any extra motivation for facing Milan?

“In any case, I spent four years at Inter, and it was a very wonderful and notable experience. It’s a great experience to be able to play against Milan, but for me the most important thing is the three points from the win. That’s my goal.”.

Does the fact that this is a crucial match for Milan in terms of the league position provide additional motivation for Olympiacos to remain focused?

Industry observers note that “It’s an notable match for both Milan and Olympiacos, even though we have ten points. We’ll do everything we can to get the points we need to win and reach thirteen. We’ll give our all to achieve that.”.

Could this match also be a calling card for you for the Italian national team? Also, how much have Milan changed since you faced them with Inter?

“Considering that I’ve been here for almost three years and that my career is going well, I don’t see the match against Milan as a positive or negative opportunity for the national team.

“Milan are always a dangerous team and has a good squad. Anything can happen in a match, and as I’ve stated before, we’ll do everything we can to win.”.

What do you expect from Milan in tomorrow’s match, and how do you see them competing for the title?

“It will be a tough and intense match, with both teams pressing hard. I think it will be a very close game, and we’ll try to give our best. As for the league, everything is still open. We’re only at the start of the season, so I can’t give a precise assessment right now.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 13:37.
  • Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will attempt to earn a much-needed boost in the Premier League when they square off on Friday night.
  • Despite seven points separating these teams in the Premier League table, the home side are arguably the favourites to prevail from this fixture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 13:37.

Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will attempt to earn a much-needed boost in the Premier League when they square off on Friday night.

Despite seven points separating these teams in the Premier League table, the home side are arguably the favourites to prevail from this fixture.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League match will kick off at 8pm, UK time, on Saturday.

This Premier League game between Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will be held at the City Ground, the home stadium of Forest.

Last season's corresponding fixture ended in a 3-0 victory for Chelsea, albeit in a game where Forest - then with Ange Postecoglou at the helm - squandered a number of opportunities.

The Premier League contest will be available on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League for viewers in the UK.

Sky customers can access the Premier League match on Sky Go and on the Sky Sports app, while it is also available via Now TV's Sports membership.

Sky Sports will show highlights, including any goals which have been scored, on their social media and YouTube channels, as well as on their dedicated app.

Meanwhile, those wishing to watch highlights on Match of the Day will have to wait until Saturday evening, with the programme starting at 10.30pm.

Both teams head into this fixture with question marks over their physicality, an problem which Oliver Glasner addressed in his pre-match press conference.

Forest begin the latest batch of games sitting in 17th position in the Premier League table, but they can move into 14th place with victory on Friday night.

Eight teams - including Chelsea - possess a worse defensive record than Forest, emphasising the feeling that they could quickly move up the standings if they resolve their issues in the final third.

On the back of three defeats in four matches and with 20 goals conceded in 11 games, Chelsea will be perceived to be ideal opponents for Forest.

While Chelsea have the opportunity to move into fifth place, they are highly likely to end the weekend in the bottom half of the table should they lose in the East Midlands.

#129248. Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 47m • 📚 Deep Dive (9334 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 47 min read (9334 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~47 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges1.
  • Sources indicate that photoconversion processes underpin technologies ranging from photodetection and photovoltaics to photoemission and photochemistry.
  • Industry observers note that recent studies have shown that hot carriers can be manipulated using ultrafast spin exchange (SE) interactions in manganese (Mn)-doped colloidal quantum dots (QDs)10,11,12.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges1. Here we demonstrate a spin-exchange-driven phototransport regime in manganese-doped quantum dot films that enables the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers. Ultrafast spin-exchange-mediated Auger upconversion promotes electrons into high-energy, delocalized states before phonon cooling2,3, establishing a transient high-mobility conduction channel. Crucially, spin-exchange interactions not only generate hot carriers but also enable their repeated re-excitation, thereby sustaining long-range drift. This mechanism yields room-temperature mobilities of about 150 cm2 V−1 s−1 and submillimetre drift lengths—far greater than those of conventional quantum dot solids and approaching values characteristic of crystalline semiconductors. Time-of-flight measurements confirm drift-dominated transport, with transit times scaling linearly with distance and inversely with electric field. These results establish a route to long-range energy transport in nanoscale materials and enable the use of hot carriers in photoconversion, photochemistry and transit-time-limited photodetection.

Sources indicate that photoconversion processes underpin technologies ranging from photodetection and photovoltaics to photoemission and photochemistry. Their ability to exploit excess photon energy is limited by rapid phonon-assisted cooling of nonequilibrium (‘hot’) carriers to band-edge states, typically within picoseconds, severely restricting their lifetime and transport range. Stabilizing and transporting hot carriers therefore remains a substantial challenge for advanced solar-energy conversion4,5,6,7 and high-energy photochemistry8,9.

Industry observers note that recent studies have shown that hot carriers can be manipulated using ultrafast spin exchange (SE) interactions in manganese (Mn)-doped colloidal quantum dots (QDs)10,11,12. These interactions mediate subpicosecond Auger-type energy transfer between QD excitons and Mn spin states, reaching energy-transfer rates of about 10 eV ps−1 (ref. 11), well above typical phonon-related energy-loss rates (≲1 eV ps−1)13,14. By outcompeting intraband cooling, SE-Auger processes provide an efficient pathway for harvesting hot-electron energy, enabling phenomena such as visible-light generation of solvated electrons2,15 and carrier multiplication12.

According to recent reports, here we demonstrate that SE-Auger upconversion in Mn-doped QD films promotes photoelectrons into high-energy, delocalized transport states, enabling rapid, long-range hot-carrier transport through the QD solid. Transient photocurrent (TPC) measurements reveal time-of-flight (ToF) dynamics with drift mobilities of about 150 cm2 V−1 s−1 and submillimetre transport distances—well beyond those typically observed in QD solids. These results establish a route to long-range hot-carrier transport for photoconversion and hot-electron-driven photochemistry.

We prepared undoped (reference) and Mn-doped CdSe QDs overcoated with a thin protective CdS shell (Methods). We focus on CdSe/CdS QDs with an initial core radius of rCdSe ≈ 1.65 nm. The undoped sample exhibits a photoluminescence (PL) peak at about 2.15 eV and a band-edge (1S) absorption feature at about 2.23 eV (Fig. 1a, black curves).

a, Absorption (solid lines) and PL (dashed lines) spectra of undoped (black), lightly doped (blue) and heavily doped (red) QDs. The orange arrow marks the internal Mn spin-flip transition (EMn = 2.1 eV). Insets, schematics of undoped (top), lightly doped (middle) and heavily doped (bottom) CdSe/CdS QDs. In the heavily doped sample, an interfacial MnxCd1−xSe barrier layer forms between the CdSe core and CdS shell. b, PL dynamics of undoped (black), lightly doped (blue) and heavily doped (red) QDs. Single-exponential fits to the undoped and lightly doped traces (dashed lines) yield τPL,0 = 35 ns and τPL,Mn = 61 ns, respectively; a double-exponential fit to the heavily doped trace (dashed red line) gives an average lifetime of ⟨τPL,Mn⟩ = 225 ns. Inset, forward (time constant τF, solid black arrows) and backward (τB, dashed black arrows) SE-driven excitation transfer between the QD exciton and Mn spin excitation. Short red arrows indicate the spin orientation of electrons (filled red circles); for holes (open red circles), the arrow denotes the spin of the electron removed to create the hole. c, Tail-normalized band-edge bleach dynamics of the undoped sample as a function of ⟨N⟩, the average number of excitons generated per QD per pulse; ΔαBE is the pump-induced change in the band-edge absorption coefficient. At ⟨N⟩ ≳ 1, a fast component emerges owing to multiexciton Auger recombination, illustrated in the bottom inset for a biexciton (XX). Top inset, biexciton dynamics obtained by subtracting tail-normalized traces measured at ⟨N⟩ = 1.32 and 0.19 (circles); a single-exponential fit (line) gives τA = 85 ps. d, Corresponding dynamics for lightly doped QDs show strongly accelerated decay owing to SE-Auger recombination (note the 8-ps time window compared with 800 ps in c). The SE-Auger lifetimes of hybrid biexciton (X–Mn*) and triexciton (XX–Mn*) states, extracted using the subtraction procedure (top inset), are τSE-A = 0.91 ps and 0.23 ps, respectively. The SE-Auger process is illustrated in the bottom inset. All measurements were performed on QD solutions in toluene; time-resolved PL and TA measurements used 150-fs, 2.4-eV excitation pulses. a.u., arbitrary units.

Mn-doped samples were synthesized by diffusion doping of the CdSe cores, involving partial Cd2+ → Mn2+ cation exchange near the surface followed by Mn diffusion into the core interior16,17 (Methods). The Mn content was controlled by the doping time (tMn = 5–30 min). Here we examine samples prepared with tMn = 10 and 20 min, referred to as ‘lightly’ and ‘heavily’ doped QDs, respectively.

Recent findings suggest that the lightly doped QDs show spectral features similar to those of the undoped reference (Fig. 1a, blue curves), indicating no appreciable change in the effective CdSe core size. The heavily doped sample exhibits an approximately 130-meV blue shift of both PL and absorption (Fig. 1a, red curves), consistent with a reduction of the effective CdSe core radius to about 1.35 nm owing to formation of a higher-bandgap MnxCd1−xSe surface layer.

Mn incorporation strongly modifies single-exciton PL dynamics measured at low excitation levels (⟨N⟩ < 0.1, in which ⟨N⟩ is the average number of excitons generated per QD per pulse). The PL lifetime increases from τPL,0 = 35 ns in undoped QDs to τPL,Mn = 61 ns in lightly doped QDs and to an average of 225 ns in heavily doped QDs (Fig. 1b).

In a recent development, this behaviour arises from ultrafast (subpicosecond) bidirectional SE-mediated excitation transfer between the QD exciton (X) and the internal Mn spin-flip transition (EMn = 2.1 eV)2,10,18. In the forward process, the QD exciton relaxes while promoting the Mn ion from the spin-up 6A1 ground state to the spin-down 4T1 state (Fig. 1b, inset). This occurs through two concerted spin-conserving transfers: a spin-up Mn 3d electron fills the QD valence-band (VB) hole, while a spin-down QD conduction-band (CB) electron is simultaneously transferred into the Mn 3d shell. In the reverse process, spin-flip relaxation of the excited Mn ion (Mn*) regenerates a QD exciton.

Industry observers note that the rapid forward and backward transfers establish a quasi-steady-state distribution between excitonic and Mn-based states, with occupation probabilities pX and pMn related by pX/pMn = exp[−(ΕX − ΕMn)/δ0], in which ΕX is the exciton energy (determined from the PL peak energy) and δ0 = 103 meV is an experimentally determined characteristic energy3,11. Because the intrinsic Mn* lifetime is very long (τMn ≳ 1 ms; ref. 18), decay of the coupled X–Mn system is governed by its excitonic component, 1/τPL,Mn ≈ pX/τPL,0.

For the lightly doped sample, in which EMn ≈ EX, pX ≈ pMn, giving τPL,Mn ≈ 2τPL,0 ≈ 70 ns, close to the measured 61 ns. For the heavily doped sample (ΕX − ΕMn = 188 meV), the model yields τPL,Mn ≈ 7.2τPL,0 ≈ 252 ns, again close to the observed 225 ns. The prolonged lifetime of the coupled X–Mn excitation facilitates multiexciton formation and thereby supports the SE-Auger processes underlying the long-range hot-electron transport discussed below.

Although slowing single-exciton decay, Mn doping greatly accelerates multiexciton dynamics, which in undoped QDs are governed by Auger recombination, for which electron–hole recombination energy is transferred to a third carrier within the same QD19 (Fig. 1c, bottom inset). In the undoped sample, this process appears as a fast decay component in transient absorption (TA) traces (Methods), emerging near ⟨N⟩ ≈ 1 (Fig. 1c). From this component, we extract a biexciton Auger lifetime of τA = 85 ps (Fig. 1c, top inset).

In Mn-doped QDs, the TA decay also accelerates near ⟨N⟩ ≈ 1 (Fig. 1d, lightly doped sample), but the corresponding time constant is nearly two orders of magnitude shorter, about 910 fs, and decreases further to about 230 fs at higher excitation levels (Fig. 1d, top inset). These subpicosecond dynamics arise from SE-Auger recombination of hybrid multiexciton states comprising intrinsic QD excitons and excited Mn ions2,3. In the electron re-excitation pathway (Fig. 1d, bottom inset), two concerted spin-transfer events promote a spin-down Mn 3d electron into a hot QD CB state, whereas the Mn ion is restored to its ground-state configuration by transfer of a spin-up electron from the QD band-edge CB state. As a result, the hot electron is elevated above the QD band edge by EMn.

Previous studies established that the SE-Auger rate depends mainly on exciton multiplicity and only weakly on the number of excited Mn ions3. Accordingly, the observed time constants of 910 and 230 fs are consistent with SE-Auger decay of hybrid biexciton (X–Mn*) and triexciton (XX–Mn*) states, respectively3.

A key consequence is the very high energy-gain rate associated with SE-Auger upconversion (rgain). For τSE-A = 230 fs, rgain = rSE-A = EMn/τSE-A ≈ 9 eV ps−1, far exceeding typical phonon-assisted energy-loss rates (rphon ≲ 1 eV ps−1)13,14. Thus, SE-Auger upconversion can outcompete phonon cooling and efficiently generate and manipulate hot carriers.

A high SE-Auger upconversion rate could enable Auger-assisted hot-carrier transport with strongly enhanced photoconductance. Specifically, theory predicts that Auger excitation above the QD ionization threshold can promote electrons into delocalized, ‘quasi-free’ states with greatly increased mobility20. Experimentally, short-lived bursts of enhanced carrier mobility were previously observed in undoped PbSe QD films21 and attributed to Auger-generated hot electrons that remained confined within individual QDs. The corresponding transport range was, however, limited to the approximately 50–100-nm near-contact region. Here we use ultrafast SE-Auger interactions to promote electrons above the confinement barrier, as originally foreseen in ref. 20, and show that this enables submillimetre transport.

The concept of Auger-enhanced conductivity is illustrated in Fig. 2a. If an electron is excited above the QD confinement barrier—that is, effectively ejected from the QD—it can access a high-mobility transport band formed by closely spaced, delocalized peripheral states22. In typical CdSe QDs, however, direct ejection of a band-edge electron by a single conventional Auger upconversion step is unfavourable because the transferred energy, approximately equal to the bandgap Eg, is smaller than the confinement barrier. Ejection can still occur from higher-lying transient states (Fig. 2a) but rapid phonon cooling usually returns carriers to the band edge before Auger upconversion can take place.

Recent findings suggest that a, Schematic of Auger-assisted hot-carrier photoconductance. Absorption of an above-band-edge photon (wavy blue arrow) in a QD containing a pre-existing electron generates a multicarrier (trion) state that undergoes Auger recombination, promoting an electron into a high-energy, delocalized hot state. Access to this state requires retention of the photogenerated electron’s excess energy and is therefore efficient only when the Auger energy-transfer rate (rA) exceeds the phonon-assisted energy-loss rate (rphon). b, Schematic of the Auston switch device containing a QD film as the photoactive layer (top) and the experimental geometry (bottom). The QD film within the 70-µm gap (L) between two gold (Au) electrodes is excited by a focused laser beam whose position can be translated across the gap; d denotes the distance between the beam centre and the positive electrode. c, Photocurrent transients for the undoped sample as a function of excitation level (⟨N⟩ = 0.23–5.38). Inset, tail-normalized TPC traces for ⟨N⟩ = 0.23 and 2.00 (black); their difference (red) is fitted to a single exponential, yielding a biexciton Auger lifetime of τA = 110 ps. Measurements used 150-fs, 3.6-eV excitation pulses with the beam centred at d = 15 μm. IRF denotes the instrument response function. d, TPC traces for the heavily doped sample under identical conditions exhibit markedly different behaviour at high ⟨N⟩, developing a pronounced step-like component whose amplitude increases rapidly—approximately cubically—with ⟨N⟩ (inset). a.u., arbitrary units.

It has been revealed that owing to its ultrafast character, SE-Auger upconversion can overcome this limitation by ejecting a nonthermalized electron before it loses its excess energy to phonons11. Band-edge electrons can also be expelled from the QD through two sequential SE-Auger upconversion steps2.

According to recent reports, to investigate the role of SE interactions in phototransport, we performed TPC measurements using Auston switch devices in which undoped or Mn-doped QD films were incorporated into a 70-µm gap of a 50-Ω microstrip transmission line21,23,24,25 (Fig. 2b and Extended Data Fig. 1; Methods). The QDs were excited by 150-fs laser pulses focused into a narrow stripe (70–80 µm full width at half maximum, FWHM), whose position within the gap was varied by translating the sample. The TPC signal was recorded with a 20-GHz sampling oscilloscope, yielding an overall temporal resolution of approximately 50 ps.

Dark-conductivity measurements (Extended Data Fig. 2) show that the QD films are highly resistive at equilibrium, indicating that the TPC response is dominated by photogenerated rather than equilibrium carriers.

In most experiments, the QDs were excited at Ephot = 3.6 eV, more than 1 eV above the band edge. Under these conditions, SE-Auger interactions can efficiently eject electrons from Mn-doped QDs11, whereas ejection by means of slower conventional Auger processes in undoped QDs is much less likely. Thus, any strong enhancement of photoconductance provides a direct signature of SE-Auger-driven hot-carrier generation and transport.

According to recent reports, in Fig. 2c,d, we compare pump-intensity-dependent photocurrent transients for undoped and Mn-doped QD films, respectively, measured at a device bias of V = 100 V and Ephot = 3.6 eV.

For the undoped sample, the excitation range corresponds to ⟨N⟩ from 0.23 to 5.38 excitons per QD. Increasing pump fluence does not substantially alter the overall TPC profile; the main effect is an acceleration of the early-time decay at ⟨N⟩ ≳ 1, similar to the behaviour observed in TA measurements (Fig. 1c) and likewise indicative of multiexciton Auger recombination. A biexciton Auger lifetime extracted from the fast TPC component (about 110 ps; Fig. 2c, inset) agrees reasonably well with that obtained from TA (about 85 ps; Fig. 1c, inset).

The ⟨N⟩ dependence of both the early-time TPC peak amplitude (time t = tpeak) and the long-time signal (t = 400 ps > τA) is also well described by the Auger recombination model (Fig. 3a, black symbols and lines). In this model, the peak photocurrent contains contributions from both single-exciton and multiexciton states, whereas after Auger decay, the long-time signal originates only from single excitons (Supplementary Note 1).

In a recent development, a, Early-time peak TPC signal (open squares) and long-time (t = 400 ps; post-Auger decay) TPC amplitude (filled black circles) for the undoped sample as a function of ⟨N⟩, extracted from Fig. 2c. The data are described by a model assuming Poisson-distributed initial exciton occupancies and constant carrier mobility (black lines). For the doped sample, the TPC step amplitude at t = 400 ps (filled red circles; from Fig. 2d) increases rapidly for ⟨N⟩ > 1, indicating a strong increase in carrier mobility. The data are reproduced by a model of SE-Auger-assisted activation into a high-mobility hot-electron transport band (red line). b, Schematic of SE-Auger upconversion involving an electron in a transient above-band-edge state. This process competes with phonon-assisted relaxation (‘cooling’) at rate rphon. Efficient promotion of electrons into the hot-carrier transport band requires the SE-Auger energy-transfer rate rSE-A to exceed rphon. c, Early-time TA spectra of a heavily doped QD film (Ephot = 3.6 eV, Δt = 3 ps) for ⟨N⟩ ≲ 1 (green and blue) and ⟨N⟩ ≳ 1 (red and black). Below the SE-Auger onset, the spectra are dominated by the band-edge bleach from state filling. Above the onset, a pronounced photoinduced absorption develops below the bleach, producing the derivative-like lineshape characteristic of a carrier-induced Stark effect. Inset, SE-Auger activation into a delocalized transport state spatially separates the electron and hole wavefunctions, generating a local electric field (Feh, red arrow) that shifts the band-edge transition by ΔESt. a.u., arbitrary units.

Recent findings suggest that these results show that TPC dynamics in undoped QD films are dominated by carrier recombination, with no detectable signatures of transit across the electrode gap. The corresponding transit times are therefore much longer than the characteristic recombination times because of the low carrier mobility.

In contrast to the undoped samples, photocurrent transients from Mn-doped QD films change markedly with increasing pump fluence (Fig. 2d, heavily doped sample). At ⟨N⟩ ≳ 1, the TPC traces develop a pronounced step-like component whose amplitude grows approximately cubically with ⟨N⟩ (IPC,400ps ∝ ⟨N⟩3.05; Fig. 2d, inset), where IPC,400ps is the photocurrent amplitude measured at t = 400 ps after excitation. This superlinear growth cannot be explained by the increase in carrier population alone and instead indicates an increase in carrier mobility by orders of magnitude.

The onset of this rapid photocurrent growth coincides with the threshold for SE-Auger recombination, suggesting SE-Auger-driven activation of electrons into a higher-energy transport band above the QD confinement barrier, as proposed in ref. 20. The absence of this effect in undoped QDs further points to the critical role of ultrafast SE-Auger upconversion, which can intercept an energetic photoelectron before intraband cooling and promote it into a peripheral, delocalized state outside the QD (Fig. 3b).

The excitation-level dependence of the TPC step amplitude (evaluated at t = 400 ps) further supports its SE-Auger origin. As detailed in Supplementary Note 2, the data are well described using the previously established (n − 1)2 scaling of the SE-Auger rate with exciton multiplicity n (Fig. 3a, red symbols and line)3.

According to recent reports, further evidence for electron ejection from the QD is provided by pump-fluence-dependent TA spectra (Fig. 3c). At ⟨N⟩ < 1, the spectra are dominated by a state-filling bleach at 2.34 eV, whereas at ⟨N⟩ ≳ 1, they evolve into a derivative-like lineshape characteristic of electron ejection11,26. The resulting spatial separation of the ejected electron and the hole remaining in the QD generates an internal electric field (Fig. 3c, inset) that redshifts the band-edge transition through the Stark effect, producing induced absorption below the original bleach.

In a recent development, A step-like TPC signal with an abrupt cut-off is a hallmark of ToF photocurrent observed in high-mobility photoconductors, in which photocarriers are rapidly swept from the photoconductive gap by drift towards the electrodes27,28,29. In this regime, the photocurrent duration is determined not by carrier relaxation but by the carrier transit time, ttr = d/vd = d/(μF), in which d is the transport distance, vd the drift velocity, μ the carrier mobility and F the electric field.

According to recent reports, to test for ToF transport in Mn-doped QD films, we measured photocurrent transients as a function of both transport distance and electric field, F = V/L, in which L = 70 μm is the electrode gap. Figure 4a indicates TPC traces for heavily doped QDs at three distances from the positive electrode, d = 15, 45 and 65 µm. The TPC pulse duration increases systematically with d, a defining signature of carrier transit27 and evidence that the photoresponse is dominated by high-mobility hot electrons generated by SE-Auger upconversion2,30,31.

Recent findings suggest that a, TPC traces for heavily doped QDs measured at V = 100 V, Ephot = 3.6 eV and ⟨N⟩ = 5.12 (solid lines) for d = 15 µm (red), 45 µm (blue) and 65 µm (green). Dashed lines are fits to the ToF model, yielding vd = 24 µm ns−1, 22 µm ns−1 and 13 µm ns−1, respectively, with τ0 = 7 ns. Inset, transit time as a function of d, determined from the inflection points of log–log TPC plots (symbols) for V = 100 V (red) and 70 V (black). Linear fits (lines) yield vd = 21.5 ± 0.4 µm ns−1 and 15.3 ± 0.4 µm ns−1, respectively. b, Model of hot-electron transport with SE-Auger generation and regeneration. SE-Auger recombination of a hybrid biexciton promotes an electron into a high-mobility transport band above the QD confinement barrier. During drift, the hot electron may partially relax into internal QD states, from which it can be re-excited into the transport band by SE-Auger energy transfer from a long-lived excited Mn ion, sustaining long-range transport. a.u., arbitrary units.

The complementary holes remain largely confined within the CdSe cores and are not expected to contribute appreciably to the fast TPC response. However, we do not detect persistent charge accumulation in the photoconductive gap, probably because the non-zero dark conductivity of the QD films (Extended Data Fig. 2) enables charge neutralization between successive excitation pulses.

The measured TPC profiles are well described by the error-function form of the ToF expression for a Gaussian photoexcitation profile (dashed lines in Fig. 4a; Supplementary Note 3 and Extended Data Fig. 3). Minor deviations include an initial capacitive spike29,32 and a weak long-time tail associated with delayed electrons, discussed below.

Modelling of the d = 15 μm trace yields a drift velocity of vd = 24 μm ns−1 and an effective lifetime τ0 = 7 ns. In conventional ToF models, τ0 describes recombination and/or trapping of mobile carriers. Here it instead represents the effective lifetime of the high-mobility hot-electron population. Whereas hot electrons normally cool to the band edge within a few picoseconds14,33, in Mn-doped QDs, their lifetime is extended by SE-Auger regeneration (Fig. 4b). Long-lived Mn excitations persist during carrier transit and can repeatedly re-excite partially relaxed electrons into the transport band before complete cooling. Regeneration is imperfect, however: if a relaxing electron encounters a QD lacking an excited Mn ion or otherwise unable to support SE-Auger re-excitation, it relaxes into a low-mobility band-edge state. Thus, τ0 represents the average survival time of the regenerated hot-electron population.

According to recent reports, toF fits at longer transport distances yield an apparent decrease in vd from 24 μm ns−1 at d = 15 μm to 13 μm ns−1 at d = 65 μm, whereas τ0 remains essentially unchanged (Fig. 4a). We attribute this reduction to the increasing contribution of delayed electrons that progressively lose mobility as regeneration becomes less effective, broadening the trailing edge of the TPC transient. The shortest-distance value, vd = 24 μm ns−1, therefore provides the best estimate of the intrinsic drift velocity of the regenerated hot-electron population.

Recent findings suggest that we also estimate the transit time with the commonly used empirical approach, in which ttr is identified from the inflection point of a log–log TPC plot, determined from the intersection of power-law fits to the pre-transit and post-transit regions27,28,34,35 (Fig. 5a). The resulting ttr values scale linearly with d (Fig. 4a, inset), as expected for ToF transport. The slope yields vd = 21.5 ± 0.4 µm ns−1, in good agreement with the value obtained from error-function modelling of the d = 15 μm trace (vd = 24 µm ns−1).

Recent findings suggest that at a lower bias (V = 70 V), ttr again scales linearly with d (Fig. 4a, inset and Extended Data Fig. 4), yielding vd = 15.3 ± 0.4 µm ns−1. The ratio of drift velocities at 70 V and 100 V (0.71) closely matches the voltage ratio (0.7), confirming the expected linear dependence of vd on electric field. Bias-dependent measurements at fixed distances (d = 45 µm and 25 µm; Fig. 5b and Extended Data Fig. 5) provide an independent test: ttr increases with decreasing bias following the expected 1/V dependence (Fig. 5c).

a, Log–log plot of distance-dependent TPC traces measured for a heavily doped QD film at V = 100 V under 3.6-eV excitation with ⟨N⟩ = 5.12. The traces are vertically offset for clarity. Straight dashed lines show power-law fits to the pre-transit and post-transit regions of the uppermost TPC trace. Their intersection defines the carrier transit time ttr (red diamonds). b, Bias-dependent TPC traces measured at d = 45 µm under the same excitation conditions. Carrier transit times determined from the inflection points of the log–log traces are indicated by red diamonds. c, Transit time ttr versus bias V for d = 45 µm (open black squares) and 25 µm (filled red circles). Fits to ttr = (1/µe)(dL/V) yield electron mobilities of µe = 144 cm2 V−1 s−1 and 156 cm2 V−1 s−1, respectively. d, Transit time versus d/F combining distance-dependent (green and red symbols) and bias-dependent (black and blue symbols) measurements. The d/F axis is multiplied by 10 so that, with ttr in ns and d/F in µm2 V−1, the slope directly equals 1/µe for µe expressed in cm2 V−1 s−1. The data follow the expected linear dependence for ToF transport (line), yielding an average electron drift mobility of ⟨µe⟩ = 150 ± 11 cm2 V−1 s−1. The shaded region represents the one-standard-error uncertainty of the fitted mobility. a.u., arbitrary units.

In a recent development, figure 5d summarizes all distance-dependent and bias-dependent measurements (25 data points) by plotting ttr versus d/F, with the horizontal axis scaled by a factor of 10 for convenient unit conversion, as described in the figure caption. For ToF transport, ttr = d/vd = (1/µ)(d/F), so the data should follow a straight line with slope 1/µ. The experimental data indeed collapse onto a single linear trend (Fig. 5d, black line), yielding an average electron mobility of ⟨µe⟩ = 150 ± 11 cm2 V−1 s−1, consistent with values obtained independently from the distance-dependent and bias-dependent data (Fig. 4a, inset and Fig. 5c).

It has been revealed that the ToF behaviour is reproducible across independently synthesized QD batches and several Auston switch devices. Further measurements yield electron mobilities of around 150–170 cm2 V−1 s−1 (Extended Data Fig. 6), confirming the robustness of the high-mobility hot-electron transport regime.

Although the present study focuses on 3.6-eV excitation, long-range hot-electron transport is also observed under near-band-edge excitation at 2.4 eV (Extended Data Fig. 7). In this case, the onset of the rapid TPC increase shifts from ⟨N⟩ ≈ 1 to ⟨N⟩ ≈ 2, consistent with the SE-Auger ionization model. Because ejection of a near-band-edge electron requires two sequential SE-Auger upconversion steps, ionization occurs only once three excitons are generated, in agreement with previous observations of SE-driven photoionization2. Above this threshold, the transport characteristics are essentially unchanged: bias-dependent and distance-dependent TPC measurements exhibit the same ToF behaviour and yield ⟨μe⟩ = 164 cm2 V−1 s−1, close to the value obtained under 3.6-eV excitation.

Industry observers note that the measured drift mobility, ⟨μe⟩ ≈ 150 cm2 V−1 s−1, is about an order of magnitude higher than values typically reported for strongly coupled, device-grade QD films (10–20 cm2 V−1 s−1) (refs. 1,36) and approaches the room-temperature electron drift mobilities of bulk wide-bandgap II–VI semiconductors (approximately 200–600 cm2 V−1 s−1) (ref. 37). This comparison serves only as a benchmark of mobility magnitude and does not imply equivalent transport mechanisms or device operation.

The high hot-electron mobility also enables long transport distances. Using τ0 = 7 ns and vd = 21.5 µm ns−1 (V = 100 V) gives a drift range of about 0.15 mm. Such transport distances are extraordinary for colloidal QD solids and place Mn-doped QD films in a transport regime more commonly associated with crystalline semiconductors than with ligand-linked nanocrystal assemblies. Collectively, these results demonstrate a high-mobility transport regime in which SE-Auger excitation promotes photoelectrons into a delocalized hot-carrier transport band, whereas repeated SE-Auger regeneration sustains their long-range drift (Fig. 4b).

According to recent reports, we report a phototransport regime in which SE-Auger upconversion dynamically promotes electrons into a delocalized, high-mobility band above the QD confinement barrier, yielding carrier mobilities of about 150 cm2 V−1 s−1 and submillimetre transport distances. Unlike conventional band-like transport, this mechanism does not rely on miniband formation or strong electronic coupling between neighbouring QDs. Instead, repeated SE-Auger activation regenerates high-energy transport states following partial relaxation, sustaining hot-electron transport over nanosecond timescales.

According to recent reports, long-range hot-electron transport can enable transit-time-limited photodetection in the GHz regime, ultrafast optical-to-electrical signal conversion and modulation and electrical sampling of ultrafast optical signals. Beyond optoelectronics, SE-enabled stabilization and transport of hot carriers offer a strategy for harnessing high-energy electrons in photochemical processes. Their high mobility, expanded wavefunctions and strong reducing power make them attractive as both energetic charge carriers and agents of remote chemical transformations.

Cadmium oxide (CdO, 99.99%, Aldrich), octadecylphosphonic acid (ODPA, 99%, PCI), trioctylphosphine oxide (TOPO, 99%, Aldrich), trioctylphosphine (TOP, 97%, Aldrich), diphenylphosphine (DPP, 98%, Aldrich), selenium (Se, 200 mesh, 99.999%, Alfa Aesar), 1-octadecene (ODE, 90%, Aldrich), oleic acid (OA, 90%, Aldrich), oleylamine (OAm, 70%, Aldrich), manganese(II) acetate tetrahydrate (Mn(ac)2·4H2O, 99.999%, Strem) and tributylphosphine (TBP, 95%, Aldrich) were used as received.

In a recent development, cdSe core particles with a wurtzite crystal structure were synthesized following a previously reported method17. Specifically, 100 mg of CdO, 490 mg of ODPA and 5 g of TOPO were loaded into a three-neck flask and degassed under vacuum at 150 °C for 1 h. Under nitrogen flow, the mixture was heated to 320 °C and maintained at this temperature until it formed a clear solution. Subsequently, 1 ml of TOP was swiftly injected into the flask. After the temperature increased to 380 °C, 1 ml of a 1.4 M TOP–Se solution was rapidly injected. At this stage, 1 mol% of DPP was added to the TOP–Se solution to control the growth kinetics17. After 3 min, the reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature by removing the heating mantle.

The resulting nanocrystals were collected by adding ethanol followed by centrifugation at 8,000 rpm. This washing procedure was repeated three times. The purified nanocrystals were then redispersed in toluene.

In a recent development, to incorporate Mn into the synthesized CdSe nanocrystals, we used a diffusion-doping procedure16 following a refined protocol of ref. 17. To remove residual Cd species, the pre-synthesized CdSe nanocrystals dispersed in toluene were precipitated with ethanol. 75 mg of the precipitate was dissolved in a mixture of 27 ml of degassed ODE and 2.7 ml of OA. The mixture was heated to 60 °C under vacuum for 1 h. After cooling to room temperature, the nanocrystals were again precipitated with ethanol and collected by centrifugation at 8,000 rpm. The resulting precipitate was added to a mixture of 510 mg of Se, 3 ml of degassed ODE and 3 ml of TBP.

Recent findings suggest that separately, 90 mg of Mn(ac)2·4H2O, 45 ml of ODE, 1.8 ml of OA and 3.9 ml of OAm were loaded into a flask and degassed under vacuum at 100 °C for 1 h. Under nitrogen flow, the mixture was heated to 300 °C, after which the previously prepared CdSe nanocrystal/TBP–Se solution in ODE was swiftly injected. The reaction temperature was maintained at 300 °C and the doping level was controlled by the reaction time (typically 5–30 min). After completion of the reaction, the mixture was cooled to room temperature. Magnetic circular dichroism measurements indicated approximately 2–5 internal Mn2+ dopants per QD, depending on the doping time17.

Owing to the large abundance of surface trap states, as-prepared Mn-doped CdSe cores do not exhibit detectable PL. To suppress surface defects, the cores were coated with a CdS shell following procedures reported in ref. 17.

In a recent development, to prepare a Cd-oleate precursor solution, 123 mg of CdO, 2.45 ml of OA and 10.8 ml of ODE were loaded into a flask and degassed at 100 °C under vacuum for 1 h. Under nitrogen flow, the temperature was increased to 250 °C and maintained for 1 h until a clear solution formed. The precursor solution was then cooled to 100 °C and maintained at this temperature until injection during CdS shell growth.

A TOP–S precursor solution was prepared by stirring a mixture of 18 ml of TOP and 44.3 mg of sulfur powder overnight in a glovebox.

It has been revealed that for shell growth, 75 mg of Mn-doped CdSe QDs were dissolved in a mixture of 28 ml of ODE, 2.4 ml of OAm and 1.2 ml of OA. This mixture was degassed at 100 °C under vacuum for 1 h. Under nitrogen flow, the flask was heated to 220 °C and 0.4-ml aliquots of the Cd-oleate and TOP–S precursor solutions were alternately injected dropwise at intervals of 2.5 min for two cycles.

A 100-nm gold layer was evaporated onto the backside of a 1-mm glass substrate to serve as the ground plane. An approximately 200-nm-thick film of undoped (reference) or Mn-doped CdSe/CdS QDs was then deposited on the top surface of the substrate through repeated spin-coating cycles, accompanied by ligand exchange and rinsing steps. During deposition, QDs dispersed in octane (20 mg ml−1) were spin-coated at 1,600 rpm for 30 s.

According to recent reports, to facilitate interdot charge transport, the QDs were cross-linked by means of solid-state ligand exchange, replacing the original long-chain ligands with short bifunctional 1,2-ethanedithiol (EDT) molecules. For ligand exchange, 60 µl of a 1 M EDT solution in methanol (MeOH) was dropped onto the QD layer, allowed to soak for 60 s and then spin-coated at 1,200 rpm for 30 s.

Industry observers note that the film was subsequently rinsed by spin-coating pure MeOH to remove excess ligands. These three steps—QD deposition, ligand exchange and rinsing—were repeated five times to obtain a QD layer approximately 200 nm thick. The resulting film was annealed at 150 °C for 30 min.

According to recent reports, finally, two 200-nm-thick gold contacts separated by a 70-µm gap were deposited on top of the QD film through a shadow mask. Together with the gold ground plane on the backside of the substrate, these contacts form a microstrip transmission line with a nominal impedance of 50 Ω.

To verify that ligand exchange and film fabrication preserved the quantum-confined electronic structure of the QDs, we performed further TA measurements on 200-nm-thick Mn-doped CdSe/CdS QD films prepared using the same ligand-exchange procedure as used for the TPC devices. The TA spectra of the film samples were compared with those of the corresponding QDs in solution under identical excitation conditions (3.6-eV, 150-fs excitation; ⟨N⟩ = 0.3). The results are presented in Extended Data Fig. 8.

Recent findings suggest that to characterize the equilibrium electrical properties of the ligand-exchanged QD films, further dark-conductivity measurements were performed using 120-nm-thick Mn-doped CdSe/CdS QD films deposited on glass substrates and contacted by thermally evaporated interdigitated Au electrodes comprising 25 pairs of 2-mm-long fingers separated by 10 μm. The corresponding current–voltage characteristics are presented in Extended Data Fig. 2.

Electrostatic simulations of the Auston switch geometry were performed using the Electrostatics interface of COMSOL Multiphysics to calculate the electric-field distribution, effective gap capacitance and effective RC constant (Extended Data Fig. 1).

In a recent development, TA measurements were performed using a standard pump–probe set-up in which absorption changes induced by a short pump pulse were probed in both the temporal and spectral domains using variably delayed probe pulses. The TA system was built around a regeneratively amplified ytterbium-doped potassium gadolinium tungstate (Yb:KGW) femtosecond laser (PHAROS, Light Conversion) generating approximately 190-fs pulses at 1.2 eV.

The laser output was split into two beams. One beam seeded a harmonic generator (HIRO HHG, Light Conversion) to produce second (2.4-eV) or third (3.6-eV) harmonic pump pulses, whose duration was shortened to about 150 fs owing to nonlinear optical pulse compression. Pulses from the second beam were delayed relative to the pump using an optical delay line (up to 5 ns) and focused onto a 3-mm-thick sapphire plate to generate broadband probe pulses in the form of a femtosecond white-light continuum.

Recent findings suggest that the pump beam was focused onto the sample into a spot with a diameter of about 120 µm, whereas the smaller-diameter probe beam (<90 µm) was centred near the middle of the pump spot. Probe pulses transmitted through the sample were detected using an Avantes AvaSpec-Fast ULS1350F-USB2 spectrometer. The measured TA spectra were corrected for chirp (spectrally dependent delay within the white-light continuum probe pulses) using the procedure described in ref. 2.

In Auger recombination studies of undoped and Mn-doped QDs, we monitored the pump-induced band-edge absorption bleach (ΔαBE), which tracks the decay of band-edge excitonic populations14.

It has been revealed that to minimize sample degradation during TPC measurements, the fabricated Auston switch devices were mounted in a nitrogen-filled, airtight chamber equipped with optical windows and electrical feedthroughs. Under these conditions, no measurable changes in the TPC response were observed during the complete characterization of a device, including pump-fluence-dependent, transport-distance-dependent and bias-dependent measurements.

It has been revealed that the chamber was mounted on a translation stage, allowing the laser beam position within the electrode gap to be varied. One of the top gold electrodes was biased using a DC power supply (Keithley 2430), whereas the other electrode was connected to a 20-GHz-bandwidth sampling oscilloscope by means of a coaxial cable. To minimize timing jitter, the oscilloscope was triggered by electrical pulses generated by a high-speed Si photodetector driven by a portion of the laser beam split from the excitation path.

Sources indicate that the QDs within the photoconductive gap of the Auston switch were excited at 2.4 eV or 3.6 eV using 150-fs pulses of the second or third harmonic of an amplified Yb:KGW femtosecond PHAROS laser, respectively. The laser beam was focused with a cylindrical achromatic lens into a narrow stripe aligned with the edges of the top gold electrodes. The spatial profile of the excitation beam was approximately Gaussian, with a stripe width of about 70–80 µm (FWHM), measured with a beam profiler. The excitation position within the photoconductive gap of the Auston switch was varied by translating the sample in a plane perpendicular to the laser beam. The position was initially calibrated using a beam profiler and monitored in real time on the sample with a CMOS camera.

According to recent reports, as discussed in Supplementary Note 3, the nonlinear dependence of SE-Auger upconversion on excitation density narrows the lateral spatial profile of the mobile hot-electron population relative to the laser beam profile (Extended Data Fig. 9). Across the film thickness, the initial hot-electron population is weighted towards the illuminated surface. However, because the optical absorption length is comparable with the QD film thickness, excited Mn ions are generated throughout the layer. Consequently, SE-Auger regeneration remains active across the film thickness, even if the hot-electron population spreads vertically during transit within the photoconductive gap.

The vertical electric field is negligible over nearly the entire photoconductive gap and becomes appreciable only within approximately 1 μm of the electrode edges. By contrast, the horizontal electric field remains nearly uniform across the gap, with an average value within 10–15% of the nominal field F = V/L. These calculations confirm that the electric field is predominantly horizontal, thereby validating the one-dimensional drift approximation used in the charge transport analysis. The computed electrostatic field distribution yields an effective gap capacitance of approximately 0.2 pF, corresponding to an estimated RC time constant of 10 ps for a 50-Ω transmission line. This value is shorter than the experimental temporal resolution of the TPC measurements (about 50 ps), indicating that the measured response is limited not by the device RC constant but by other components of the measurement circuit and the oscilloscope.

The measurements were performed on a 120-nm-thick Mn-doped CdSe/CdS QD film deposited on a glass substrate and contacted by thermally evaporated interdigitated Au electrodes comprising 25 pairs of 2-mm-long fingers separated by 10 μm. The measured current exhibits a linear dependence on the applied bias over the investigated voltage range (±60 V), corresponding to maximum electric fields of approximately 6 V μm−1, about four times larger than those used in the TPC experiments. The absence of measurable nonlinearity indicates no detectable contact-limited (Schottky) behaviour under these conditions. The extracted film resistivity is approximately 2.2 × 1010 Ω cm, demonstrating that the ligand-exchanged QD films are highly insulating at equilibrium and therefore contain only a negligible concentration of free carriers.

Blue and red traces correspond to vd = 10 µm ns−1 and d = 45 µm (blue line), vd = 20 µm ns−1 and d = 45 µm (solid red line) and vd = 20 µm ns−1 and d = 25 µm (dashed red line). The onset of the rapid TPC increase shifts from ⟨N⟩ ≈ 1 for 3.6-eV excitation to ⟨N⟩ ≈ 2 for 2.4-eV excitation, consistent with hot-electron generation by means of single-step and two-step SE-Auger upconversion, respectively. Kepa was selected ahead of the Arsenal no1 in the Carabao Cup final last March having started every previous round of the competition.

The former Chelsea shot stopper gifted City their opening goal that afternoon, dropping a cross into the path of Nico O’Reilly who headed home.

Former striker Dickov, who began his career at Arsenal before achieving legend status at City, believes Raya will be a massive loss for the champions this weekend. While convinced Arteta has full trust in Kepa, he suggests Arsenal’s backline will privately have concerns.

‘The one thing City will definitely be looking at is the loss of David Raya who is the best goalkeeper in the world for me,’ Dickov told Metro via Casino.com Ireland.

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 13:47.

Both beaten 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone and Parma will aim to bounce back when they clash at Stadio Benito Stirpe on Saturday.

Despite suffering consecutive defeats for the first time this term, the hosts are still 12 points above their visitors in the Serie A standings.

Frosinone made an unexpectedly strong start to their latest comeback campaign, scoring freely while winning six of their first 11 fixtures after returning to Serie A.

However, Massimiliano Alvini's attack-minded side then suffered a rare setback, going down 1-0 to Cagliari, before they were well beaten just after the international break.

Two goals down within 20 minutes, the Canarini continued to fly forward, but they never really recovered and ultimately lost 5-1 to AC Milan at San Siro.

In fact, Frosinone have only claimed two points on the road since beating Fiorentina at the end of August, so their form at Stadio Stirpe has kept them tucked inside the top half.

After narrowly losing their first home fixture against Juventus, they have since won all of the next five, so confidence should still be high when lowly Parma come to town.

While their promoted hosts sit seventh in Serie A, Parma are hovering above the relegation zone with just eight points on the board.

Like Frosinone, they were thumped 5-1 last week, as Roma stormed to victory at Stadio Tardini, with Capocannoniere leader Donyell Malen helping himself to four goals.

That was the Gialloblu's eighth defeat from their first 12 league games, and the recent hiring of their second-highest Serie A scorer has hardly had an impact.

Alberto Gilardino has only celebrated one win since succeeding Carlos Cuesta, who kept the Emilian club afloat last term, but that lone success did come on the road.

Following a run of six straight away defeats, Parma recently beat Atalanta 3-0 in Bergamo, so they will aim to claim more points when they head south on Saturday.

Now trailing Malen in the race to be crowned Italy's top scorer, Frosinone striker Antonio Raimondo is still sidelined by injury - and his deputy is also unavailable.

Daniel Birligea bagged a brace against Lecce before scoring for Romania in their recent Nations League camp, but he strained a hamstring in Milan and has been ruled out for the next few weeks.

So, it remains to be seen whether Alvini selects support forwards Fares Ghedjemis, Romano Schmid and Giorgi Kvernadze - each of whom have provided four Serie A assists - or Slovak centre-forward Tomas Bobcek to lead the hosts' attack.

On the absence front, Florian Grillitsch has yet to recover from a thigh problem, but left-back Gabriele Bracaglia can return after serving a one-match ban.

While Parma will welcome back Abdoulaye Ndiaye from suspension, Argentine striker David Romero is still ruled out by a serious shoulder injury; defensive duo Diego Carlos (thigh) and Dominik Drobnic (foot) are also doubts.

In Romero's absence, Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is also a contender after scoring the Gialloblu's lone goal against Roma.

Frosinone possible starting lineup:.

Palmisani; Oyono, Monterisi, Calvani, Bracaglia; Masini, Calo; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Bobcek.

Parma possible starting lineup:.

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Ndiaye; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Elphege, Toure.

Frosinone can arrest their decline with another home win, as Parma are in grim form and could face a long fight to avoid the drop.

Notably, the Canarini tend to start fast - scoring a league-high 11 goals inside the first 30 minutes - while their visitors have yet to score before the half-hour mark.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lee Dixon thinks Manchester City’s Premier League title chances are far from over even if they fall to defeat against Arsenal on Sunday.
  • City started the season in fine form after Enzo Maresca’s arrival, but have now slipped to third and are without a win in their last four league matches.
  • Last season’s runners-up spent lavishly over the summer, but now trail Arsenal by six points ahead of their pivotal meeting at the Emirates on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lee Dixon thinks Manchester City’s Premier League title chances are far from over even if they fall to defeat against Arsenal on Sunday.

City started the season in fine form after Enzo Maresca’s arrival, but have now slipped to third and are without a win in their last four league matches.

Last season’s runners-up spent lavishly over the summer, but now trail Arsenal by six points ahead of their pivotal meeting at the Emirates on Sunday.

Bubbling away in the background remains the possibility of a huge points deduction after the club were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges for financial breaches.

And Dixon believes that such uncertainty might be playing on the minds of City’s players, telling Metro: ‘Nobody liked Arsenal under George Graham and we built up resilience because of that.

‘I think that could have been happening for City at the start of the season with the charges, but that bounce can die off a bit and then all of a sudden, you’ve had a couple of bad results and it gets into your head.’.

Arsenal could extend their lead over City to nine points with victory at the Emirates on Sunday, but Dixon believes that it would still be far too early to rule City out of this season’s title race.

‘As a fan, after seeing Arsenal get over the line last season, you now have something to fall back on and I do believe that, from a fan’s perspective, if you see Arsenal beat City on Sunday, you can think that’s it,’ he added.

Industry observers note that ‘However, as a player, you won’t see any of them coming out and going, “It’s done and dusted”, because City have so much quality. We all know that City could go on a ten-game winning streak, so they’ll always have that opportunity.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘At the moment, there’s less pressure for Arsenal at the top from a points perspective and it’s pointing to it being their title to lose, but right now, it’s too early in the season to say it’s over if Arsenal win on Sunday.’.

Arsenal have not been at their best since returning from the international break, with a draw against Newcastle last weekend followed up by a stalemate against Borussia Dortmund in midweek.

But Dixon has still been encouraged by some aspects of Arsenal’s football, most notably the performances of Noni Madueke, who has featured more prominently since Bukayo Saka sustained a thigh injury last month.

‘I love his directness because when he comes on, his first touch is generally in the direction of the full-back which is what I hated as a full-back myself,’ Dixon noted of Madueke.

‘You know what you’re in for as a full-back coming up against somebody like him. I’ve been very impressed with him but I’ve always been worried by his end product, but he seems to be producing better numbers now.

‘You need to take your hat off to him for that because Saka’s boots are big boots to fill. He’s really had to knuckle down and he’s receiving the benefit of that.’.

Lee Dixon was speaking with Metro on behalf of Betfred.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Vancouver Whitecaps boss Jesper Sorensen acknowledged an "extremely difficult" playoff match against Real Salt Lake awaits them on Friday.

The top seed from the Western Conference won Game 1 of the best-of-three series 2-0, with Edier Ocampo and Bruno Caicedo scoring either side of half-time.

The Whitecaps, who reached the MLS Cup showpiece last year, can secure progression to the next round of the 2026 postseason with victory in Game 2 at America First Field.

Vancouver defeated FC Dallas in this round of the MLS Cup playoffs last term in two games, but were taken to penalties in Game 2.

Sorensen believes RSL will pose a serious threat and has urged his side to remember their exploits against Dallas in 2025.

"Game 2 is a tricky one for those who won Game 1; it's really about seeing if you can close it out against a team that plays with desperation, and we've seen how many teams had to go to three games to advance," Sorensen told reporters.

"This is going to be extremely difficult, but we know that we have the experience from last year in Dallas.

"In this league, it can be very difficult playing away. We're going to play up with some altitude, and we're going to play probably in some cold weather.

"It's going to be a different scenario than we played under the other day in BC, and that's what makes this league beautiful as well.

"We're facing a team that has to win this game to stay alive in the season, and we know that it's going to be a bit difficult.".

Joao Pedro remains unavailable for Chelsea’s Premier League clash with Nottingham Forest this weekend.

The Brazil international has missed his side’s last five games as a result of a thigh injury he suffered in training in October.

The former Brighton star sat out of games against Tottenham, Manchester United, Sunderland and Liverpool in the Carabao Cup with the Blues losing three of those four in his absence prior to the 4-1 hammering at home to Leeds United last weekend.

Speaking last week, Xabi Alonso revealed Pedro was still to return to training with the club assessing him ‘game by game.’.

Speaking at a press conference on Thursday ahead of the trip to Forest, Alonso was asked if any injured players would be ready to return this weekend, flatly responding: ‘No.’.

In a recent development, maxence Lacroix is also not ready to return. The former Crystal Palace star, almost ever-present at the back since his summer arrival from Crystal Palace, came off with a hamstring injury in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s one less week than from the last game,’ Alonso remarked of the Frenchman. ‘So we are closer in his recovery, but not for this game.’.

Reece James, Jorrel Hato and Jamie Gittens also remain sidelined.

There was good news on Moises Caicedo after the Ecuador international was forced off at half-time against Leeds last time out.

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for an interview not authorised by the club that caused controversy this week.

The French centre-back was strongly criticised by fans following comments made about missing a crucial penalty during Chelsea’s Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by Liverpool last month.

Fofana spoke for two-and-a-half hours with YouTuber Zack Nani, who has since insisted on social media that “several quotes were taken out of context or plainly made up in England”.

Recent findings suggest that asked about the situation at a press conference held before Friday night’s trip to Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso remarked: “We have addressed that with him [Fofana]. He has apologised.

“It was not right, he has said it is not going to be repeated, these types of things.”.

Fofana missed the decisive penalty that saw Chelsea’s Carabao Cup run end in the fourth round with a 6-5 shootout loss at Anfield following a 1-1 draw, blazing his spot-kick over the crossbar after Emmanuel Emegha had seen an effort saved by Giorgi Mamardashvili and Valentin Barco hit the woodwork.

He had also given away a penalty in normal time for handball that was converted by Cody Gakpo just three minutes after Morgan Rogers had given Chelsea the lead from 12 yards, continuing what has been a difficult season for him so far.

“The Liverpool match was tough to take, but I moved on promptly because that’s just part of football,” Fofana was quoted as saying during the interview with Nani.

“I took responsibility for the penalty - I missed it - and, well, I knew I wasn’t a good penalty taker to begin with, you know [laughs]?”.

He continued: “So, I just thought, ‘Okay, I’ll own it.’ But I ended up conceding a penalty during the match - it was a handball - but that’s just part of the game. I could have avoided it; it’s the kind of thing we talk about - you have to be consistent, and you have to keep improving in those areas.

In a recent development, “But after the penalty, I stepped up, because I’m one of the most experienced players. Out on the field, there were a lot of young guys. And, well, you had to get out there, you know?

It has been revealed that “You’ve got to go for it. And the way I look at it, if I fail, well, I’ve been through things. I’ve lived through a lot. If I fail, it’s not that it’s not a significant deal - sure, it sucks, obviously - but as for me, if I’m the one being attacked, it’s no big deal.

Sources indicate that “I sent a real beauty of a shot way over the bar. Did you see my shot? I really blasted it high [laughs]. I remember a fan, way up high, he actually managed to catch the ball. But yeah, I missed, you know.

It has been revealed that “Now, I laugh about it because it’s just part of football - that’s how it goes. And, well, there you have it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Aiming to remain unbeaten at home in the league this season, promotion-hunting Birmingham City host struggling Bolton Wanderers at St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park in the Championship on Saturday afternoon.
  • Blues were the latest side to take advantage of Burnley's Turf Moor misery on Wednesday night, whilst the Wanderers suffered defeat on their own patch by West Bromwich Albion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 13:52.

Aiming to remain unbeaten at home in the league this season, promotion-hunting Birmingham City host struggling Bolton Wanderers at St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park in the Championship on Saturday afternoon.

Blues were the latest side to take advantage of Burnley's Turf Moor misery on Wednesday night, whilst the Wanderers suffered defeat on their own patch by West Bromwich Albion.

As has been the case after each of their three Championship defeats so far this season, Birmingham City bounced back from last weekend's Stoke City disappointment by claiming three points, this time at the expense of crisis-hit Burnley.

Chris Davies's side have already equalled the number of away victories that they managed across the entirety of last season (6) courtesy of August Priske's seventh league goal of the term and an own goal from Clarets winger Jaydon Banel at Turf Moor.

Following seven wins from their past nine second-tier contests, Birmingham are occupying fourth position in the Championship table, three points behind current pacesetters Middlesbrough and Stoke.

Apart from a 6-1 battering by Brentford in the EFL Cup, Blues have been impressive at St Andrew's this season, with Saturday's hosts unbeaten across their opening eight home league battles (W4 D4).

In fact, Birmingham last experienced Second City defeat in the Championship at the beginning of April, and Davies has lost just three home league games since taking charge during the summer of 2024.

Sliding towards the relegation zone, Bolton Wanderers have now won just one of their past seven Championship contests (D2 L4) after losing to West Brom at the Toughsheet Community Stadium earlier in the week.

A second-half penalty from Ruben Rodrigues levelled the scores momentarily following Albion's opener, however, further strikes from Norwegian duo Aune Heggebo and Felix Horn Myhre sentenced the Wanderers to a fourth defeat in their past six games.

Winless in their past five games (D1 L4) at the Toughsheet, Bolton's last three victories have all arrived on the road, with Saturday's underdog visitors beating Norwich City (4-3), Wolverhampton Wanderers (3-1) and Charlton Athletic (1-0) since late September.

There is no doubting that the newly-promoted side are one of the favourites to suffer relegation this season, with Steven Schumacher's troops presently six points clear of the bottom three.

Bolton were defeated on their most recent trip to St Andrew's in October 2024 but were one of only three teams to beat Birmingham during their record-breaking League One title romp of 2024-25.

Bolton Wanderers Championship form:.

Birmingham defender Ethan Laird missed the Burnley win after picking up a knock at Stoke last weekend, with the right-back a doubt for the Second City match on Saturday.

As a result, Bright Osayi-Samuel is likely to retain his spot in defence, with Dael Fry set to drop out in order to make room for the available-again Christoph Klarer.

Liam Millar, Jhon Solis and Jay Stansfield were rested for the final 15 minutes at Turf Moor, with the trio all set to start once again this weekend.

There is likely to be alteration on the right flank, though, where Patrick Roberts could be the key to unlocking a deep Bolton block.

Bolton rotated leading marksman Sam Dalby out of the starting side on Wednesday but the Englishman is fully expected to return to the XI on Saturday.

Ben Davies could feature against his former loan employers, whilst Samuel Illing-Junior is in line for another start following a bright display against West Brom.

Birmingham City possible starting lineup:.

Wigan Athletic will be looking to continue their good form when they welcome Plymouth Argyle to the Brick Community Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts presently sit 17th in the League One table, while the visitors are eighth.

Wigan could pick up a fifth consecutive victory this weekend, having found their form in recent weeks.

After suffering four defeats in five games last month, Wigan have won five of their last six across all competitions and are unbeaten in their last four league matches.

The Latics beat managerless Blackpool 2-1 last weekend, coming from behind to earn a crucial three points thanks to goals from Jon Mellish and Finley Burns.

The result leaves Gary Caldwell's side 17th with 17 points from 16 matches, with their recent uptick in form moving them four points clear of the relegation zone.

It is also worth noting that Wigan have only lost once to Plymouth in their last eight meetings across all competitions, although that defeat was a 3-0 loss that came last season.

Plymouth, meanwhile, have endured a difficult few weeks as they back-to-back defeats in the league without scoring.

Tom Cleverley's side were beaten 3-0 away to Sheffield Wednesday before losing 2-0 at home to Peterborough United.

In fact, Plymouth have won just one of their last six league games and will be keen to get back winning ways on Saturday.

The Pilgrims remain just three points off the playoffs and Cleverley has urged his injury-hit side to "really work hard to improve".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Xabi Alonso revealed Wesley Fofana has apologised to his Chelsea team-mates for giving an interview in which he appeared to joke about his penalty miss against Liverpool.

Fofana missed the decisive spot-kick as the Blues were beaten 6-5 on spot-kicks at Anfield in the round of 16 in the EFL Cup, at the end of October.

The centre-back blazed his effort high into the stands, and he subsequently told YouTube personality Zack Nani: "I knew I wasn't a good penalty taker to begin with!".

Those comments attracted fierce criticism from sections of Chelsea's fanbase, particularly with Alonso's team sitting eighth in the Premier League following back-to-back defeats against Sunderland and Leeds United.

But ahead of Friday's trip to Nottingham Forest, the Blues boss insisted the matter was now considered closed.

Asked if he had spoken to Fofana about the interview, Alonso remarked: "Absolutely. We have addressed that with him and, for sure, it was unfortunate.

Sources indicate that "He has apologised. He knows it was not right in the moment, it was not right, the content.

"We are here to take things seriously and he has remarked it is not going to be repeated, and we know that it is something we don't want, these kinds of things.

"They are not going to be repeated, for sure.".

Happy birthday, Xabi! https://t.co/pEjttfS5ou.

— Chelsea FC (@ChelseaFC) November 25, 2026.

Since the start of March, no side has lost more Premier League games than Chelsea (13), and among ever-present clubs, only Crystal Palace (17) have earned fewer points than the Blues in that same span (23).

This season, Chelsea's Premier League games have seen more goals than those containing any other side (40 – 20 for, 20 against).

This is the earliest point in a league campaign (11 games) where the Blues have both scored and conceded 20+ goals since 1960-61 (eight games).

Asked what he put Chelsea's struggles down to, Alonso said: "There are many reasons. Football reasons, things that we can't afford to do.

It has been revealed that "The basics in football are so important to compete at this level. If you don't have those, you play as we did.

"The idea and the goal and the work and the talks have all been focused on that direction, to show a good game and to compete much better tomorrow.".

Chelsea are unbeaten in their last five away league games against Forest (W4 D1), with their current run of three consecutive victories being their best ever at the City Ground.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have already been linked with a lot of players this season.

The Anfield outfit seem to have many different areas of their first-team squad that need upgrading despite them spending well obver £600 million on latest players across the last couple of years.

These transfers were expected to set the Reds up for a while but, in reality, they just highlighted other problems that Andoni Iraola has among his ranks.

They're currently fourth in the Premier League table which, while a decent result, is far away from where they need to be.

With players such as Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz among their ranks, they should be one of the best teams in the world but, instead, they just about scraping qualification for the Champions League.

This needs to change and, with the January transfer window now just around the corner, it could be about to.

Liverpool are 'keeping a close eye' on Nico Paz.

Over the last couple of years, Liverpool's attack has been their main focus of interest in the transfer market.

Mohamed Salah, Sadio Mane and Roberto Firmino have all left now and, with Iraola at the helm, a upcoming style of football has also made its way to Anfield this term.

His heavy-metal style of play has some similarities to Jurgen Klopp's and, after two season of Arne Slot, it was a welcome re-jig.

This summer alone, over £150 million was spent with the Reds' attack taking most of the money.

But, that hasn't stopped Liverpool from being linked with even more attackers.

In fact, a fresh revision from journalist Ben Fernandes Santos has just shared that the Anfield outfit are one of the many clubs who are keeping a 'close eye' on Como's Nico Paz.

"Liverpool, Arsenal and Tottenham are keeping a close eye on Nico Paz," he wrote.

"The Argentine is focused on Como, but the summer will be crucial for his future. The trend is that he won't return to Real Madrid, despite being well liked at Valdebebas.

In a recent development, "Arda Güler's contract renewal has been unveiled, and Bellingham's will come soon. Nico knows this, and it will influence his decision.

Sources indicate that "If Real Madrid don't win any titles, they'll look to sign a creative midfielder. Mourinho is delighted with the Tchouaméni - Bernardo Silva double pivot.

"The priority remains a centre-back, with Jacobo Ramón at the top of the list.".

Nico Paz would be an unreal addition for Liverpool.

Nobody knows what Liverpool's first-team squad is going to look like in 2027.

The January transfer window is just over a month away and, with the number of players who have been linked with a switch, a huge rebuild could be on its way.

And then, in the summer, another rebuild could take place.

Paz is a highly sought-after attacker that has long been linked with a Liverpool transfer.

He's Como's best player and, the fact that he's contributed to 14 goals in the 16 games he's played this season prove how good he actually is.

Whether he's used as a number 10, a right winger or a striker, Liverpool would have an incredible player on their hands if they manage to get a deal over the line.

Here's hoping they do and the Reds add even more firepower to their already stacked attack.
