📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juventus Next Gen were beaten 4-0 at Lecco in Serie C Girone A, with three of the goals coming after half-time. Coach Massimo Brambilla admitted his young side give goals away too easily, and the table now reflects a long poor run.

At the Stadio Rigamonti-Ceppi, the manner of the defeat was as worrying as the scoreline.

The opener set the tone. Lecco needed only six minutes to go ahead. Casarotto ran through the middle, got past Corradi and beat goalkeeper Mangiapoco. Lecco held that single-goal lead until half-time.

Industry observers note that next Gen did have one clear opening before the break. In the 40th minute, Grelaud shot from near the penalty spot. Vettorel turned the effort over for a corner.

The second half was one-way traffic. Capello made it 2-0 in the 50th minute, and Manetti added a third in the 56th. Capello struck from close range after the goalkeeper parried Pellegrino’s second attempt. Murillo’s goal in the 72nd minute summed up the match. Mangiapoco erred as Juventus built from the back, and Murillo pounced.

In a recent development, the hosts are in strong form. This was their second 4-0 win in a row, after beating Dolomiti Bellunesi by the same score. Lecco have now scored 15 goals in four games.

Industry observers note that massimo Brambilla did not hide from the problems. He told TuttoMercatoWeb that his side struggled against Lecco’s high press. His players found it hard to keep the ball against a team pressing hard and man-to-man.

The coach also admitted that coming back became difficult after the second goal. He said his players must improve how they read the game and stop giving away goals so easily.

Sources indicate that the table makes the warning sharper. Brambilla’s side sit third from bottom after the defeat, having won just one of their last 12 matches.

The result also matters beyond Serie C. Carnevali has put the youth sector at the centre of the club’s aims.

In a recent development, one player supporters will watch is Destiny Elimoghale, who came off the bench at Lecco. Next Gen had started in a 3-5-2, with Durmisi and Merola in attack. Elimoghale replaced Durmisi in the 40th minute of the second half. The forward was born in 2009. His upcoming contract, announced on 3 November, runs until 30 June 2029.

Recent findings suggest that elimoghale was called up to the first-team squad for the first time on 17 September 2026. That call-up came for the opening Europa League league-phase match against NEC.

In a recent development, the next opponents arrive in good spirits. Treviso beat Novara 2-0 in round 13. Romeo scored in the 24th minute, and Paganini added the second in the 59th.

Sources indicate that the next test comes rapidly. Next Gen host Treviso in round 14 on Sunday 15 November at 17:30. A trip to Giana Erminio follows on Saturday 21 November, at the same kick-off time.

Enzo Maresca’s flawless start to the Premier League with Manchester City is over after another masterclass from Unai Emery.

Matches at Villa Park were a notoriously chastening experience for Pep Guardiola and it was the same old story for Maresca as City have now lost on their last four visits here.

On his fourth anniversary in charge of Villa, there was more tactical brilliance from Emery, who also did the double over Guardiola last season. It was Emery’s £65m record signing Nicolas Jackson who again underlined how some managers can get the best out of certain players.

Sources indicate that jackson had been a target for Emery ever since the Basque’s appointment and now has seven goals in claret and blue. It will have been an especially sweet moment for the Senegal forward, for it was Maresca who allowed him to join Bayern Munich on loan while he was in charge at Chelsea.

City’s run of seven league wins in a row always looked in danger here against a vibrant and energetic Villa. Maresca will also reflect on two poor goals conceded after errors from Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Recent findings suggest that guéhi endured a particularly difficult afternoon and was at fault for Jackson’s stunning first goal. The centre-back has struggled in recent weeks with a bad mistake in England’s defeat by Spain and he was exposed for both Ipswich goals last week. He was replaced at half-time after a booking for a foul on the excellent Jackson.

Maresca said: “I’m not worried about Marc at all, he is playing every game since the season started for us and the national team so it’s not easy. He is ok, it [taking him off] was just a technical decision and like in all games managers make changes. He was on a yellow card and sometimes one yellow card can be dangerous.”.

Recent findings suggest that when asked if the goals were avoidable, Maresca stated: “Absolutely, both. Sometimes you have to be a bit more lucky because we only conceded those two chances. We will try again to win at Villa next season. I don’t think we deserved to lose but we learn from that and move on. You can always learn something. For sure there are things we can do better today.”.

Industry observers note that while much of the focus will be on City’s 100 per cent start to the league coming to an end, Emery got everything right here. From his team selection to his set-up and substitutions, he outsmarted Maresca on many levels. After the game, Villa defender Matty Cash described his manager as “a tactical genius”.

It has been revealed that it was four years ago to the day that Emery grabbed this famous club by the shirt and collar and gave them an almighty shake. After a summer of much instability including many player sales, he appears to have already struck a formula with his newly assembled team.

There were a number of fine individual performances from many of the summer arrivals, such as Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi.

It has been revealed that emery said: “We were very motivated and Manchester City is the best team in the world so this is the level. This year we started so poorly and we needed time to understand how we improve. The players demonstrated the capacity to retrieve the level we’ve had over the last few years.

In a recent development, “Nicolas is more mature and very demanding of himself to improve. Earlier this season he was shooting over the crossbar but he is now finding the corners. There is still work to do and 11 points is not enough but we are feeling better.”.

According to recent reports, villa were fierce from the start and ahead after six minutes. Guéhi’s mistake was punished by John McGinn, with the ball dropping to Jackson who crashed a shot into the roof of the net.

The home team did require Suzuki to produce saves to stop efforts from Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov as City responded. Ndiaye also struck the outside of the post and City were level seven minutes into the second half with Erling Haaland nodding in Ndiaye’s cross at the far post. Haaland had touched the ball just eight times in the opening 45 minutes but invariably only needs one chance.

For a long time, football has a system where you can tell who deserved to win or not. It is the scoreboard. For decades, longer even, you could tell who was the better team by looking at who had the most goals.

However, football managers persist with the idea that there is another ineffable reason that decides who deserves what. Enzo Maresca is apparently no different.

Industry observers note that he told the BBC: “When we scored I had the feeling that we were in control and really for the entire game. We created many chances but unfortunately didn’t score them. We conceded one transition in the second half and they were very efficient because they scored. Bit unlucky and we learn from that.

“I was not here in the past but today I think we deserved something more.”.

Aston Villa are up to sixth with that win. However, there are six players all within three points of them below (though Ipswich played last night, of course, so have also played eight matches).

Matty Cash, speaking to TNT Sports post-match, discussed his performance which largely left Jeremy Doku quiet: “The manager gives us tasks but you have to take responsibility too, I do a lot of work on wingers, I think as a full back you have to try and get aggressive and it makes them difficult for them. Discussing Zion Suzuki’s own efforts, he added: “He’s brilliant, his first session when he came in, in the possession drill I thought we’d signed a midfielder. His vision is unbelievable, he catches crosses really well which as a full-back is a dream.”.

It has been revealed that he ended by reflecting on Unai Emery’s importance to the club, with the coach now linked with a potential vacancy at Old Trafford. Joleon Lescott tells TNT Sports: “It was a collective effort, a very impressive team performance, and the timing of the subs. Man City had a spell in the second half, got the goal, and you thought they would go on to create more chances, but Villa nullified that threat and won the game.

“Unai Emery is tactically astute, but the players still have to execute a performance.”.

Manchester City captain Ruben Dias was disappointed with an underwhelming performance.

He remarked: “Frustrating, I felt like we fought a lot. For the first 10-15 minutes of the first half we took our time to get into the game.

”They changed the way they set up so we took time to adapt. But we fought, we had chances and they ended up scoring two goals in two transitions - very efficient. Room to improve, we need to do better.

”It is what it is. Whatever happens we need to react to it. The team had a very good reaction. The second one was tough because it was very close to our equaliser. We kept going and tried to create chances. Not our day but we keep moving forward.

According to recent reports, ”I felt like we were dangerous on many occasions, even if the finish wasn’t there we arrived in dangerous places but not able to play. A word of appreciation to the boys because we kept fighting to the end.”.

Unai Emery was clear in his press conference that he sees Manchester City as one of the teams to beat this season.

He said: “They are favourites. Man City and Arsenal are so, so strong and competitive in everything. Their identity is clear. We dream of being close to them.

“Two years ago we were competing with them and Arsenal, and last December too, we were close. The gap in points is massive now this season as they have only lost once, against PSG.

“Tomorrow is a huge challenge - it is always a huge challenge against Manchester City. As a manager, I like to play games against teams like Manchester City.”.

The excellent John Percy believes that Unai Emery now can claim to be the best manager in the Premier League, with few able to match his track record.

He writes: “With Pep Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp having departed the Premier League, there can now be little doubt that Unai Emery is the best manager in England’s top division. And by some distance.

“Saturday will mark four years since Villa unveiled Emery as their head coach and few could have predicted the success that has followed. He has proved an inspired appointment who has continually embarrassed the “Massive Six” clubs.

“On every level, he has delivered: points per game, net spend, a distinguishable style of play, improving individual players, over-performance in the league and European competition.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

It has been revealed that enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

Liverpool have been constantly upgrading their team over the last couple of years.

The Anfield outfit have spent well over £600 million on new players to try and improve their ranks.

And, while some of the deal that they've struck have worked out, some still need to prove their worth.

Indeed, the performances of Liverpool's squad as a whole have improved thanks to the appointment of Andoni Iraola but, it's clear that there are still some problems that need rectifying.

Whether the Reds need to sign back-ups or replacements for their starting XI, change is needed so that they don't fall too far behind their title rivals.

So, the perfect attacker now being found by Liverpool is rather exciting.

Yunus Akgun is wanted by Liverpool.

Liverpool's attack has been one of their main focuses when improving their squad.

The Anfield outfit have spent well over £300 million on attackers alone over the last couple of years but, it still seems like the club aren't fully happy with the options that they have at their disposal.

That is obviously a crazy statement to share as, just this summer, £123 million was spent on Bradley Barcola alone.

But, with how many players Premier League clubs buy every season, there's no wonder why clubs have to constantly spend to keep up with their rivals.

And now, thanks to an update from X account Mekteb-i Gala, who have 50,000 followers, it seems like another attacker has made his way onto Liverpool's shortlist.

"EXCLUSIVE | PSG, Manchester City, Liverpool, Atletico Madrid, Como and Juventus are monitoring Yunus Akgün in every match," they wrote.

"They are in the process of gathering information on the player.".

Yunus Akgun could be an unreal back-up option for Liverpool.

Akgun is almost certainly a player that most Liverpool fans won't have heard of.

The Turkiye international is a 26-year-old winger who contributed to 21 goals across all competitions for Fenerbahce last term.

He's also had previous experience of English football as he spent the 2023-24 campaign on loan to Leicester in the Championship.

Unfortunately, his time in England didn't pan out as well as he would have hoped as he only contributed to six goals in the 29 games that he featured in.

Obviously, since most of his career has been spent in Turkiye, he probably wouldn't be able to get straight into Iraola's starting XI but, since he can play as a number 10 or a winger on either side, he could be an extremely useful back-up option for Liverpool to have.

These links are all just rumours at the moment but, of all the players who have been recently linked with Liverpool, Akgun feels like a really interesting deal for the Reds to explore, especially since they still need a back-up number 10 for Florian Wirtz.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, arsenal are in Champions League action this evening, taking on Borussia Dortmund at home.
  • He’s not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious.
  • We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had at that moment, and the first test that we’ve done showed something that is much more encouraging.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, arsenal are in Champions League action this evening, taking on Borussia Dortmund at home. It’s a game that Kepa Arrizabalaga will start in the absence of David Raya, but the news around the Arsenal number 1 was a little more positive than expected. In his press conference yesterday, Mikel Arteta said:.

He’s not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected.

We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had at that moment, and the first test that we’ve done showed something that is much more encouraging. There’s no need for surgery, which was the main fear especially because that would rule him out for months, so let’s see.

So, it seems like he’s going to miss a few games, but not anything prolonged, which is obviously good news. Elsewhere, there’s room for rotation, and I think this might be a good chance to give minutes to William Saliba who hasn’t played competitively since the World Cup. He’s had a couple of behind closed doors appearances, which will be useful in terms of fitness, but nothing compares with actually playing at this level.

It has been revealed that I wonder too if players like Ben White, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie will fancy their chances, but that seems like a lot of change in the back four – and the goalkeeper – so we’ll have to wait and see there. In midfield, we can bring Myles Lewis-Skelly in for a start, but obviously the manager has plenty to choose from in there, and up front I imagine it will be a chance for Viktor Gyokeres whose minutes have been scant so far this season. Asked if the striker had been knocking on his door about that, Arteta said:.

No, we have conversations with every player to make sure that they understand what we are doing, to gather information about the way they are feeling, and so far, it’s been very positive with Viktor and with the rest of the team.

Industry observers note that he could really use a goal tonight if he does start, as does Christos Tzolis whose numbers so far this season aren’t where you’d like them to be. Obviously there’s more to assessing a player than simply goals and assists, but for a left winger brought into replace two players who contributed a lot to the team over the last few seasons, just two assists from 11 appearances (Community Shield excluded) is a little below what you’d hope. He has had an injury, of course, but if his season needs a kick-start, tonight would be very timely.

Sources indicate that dortmund sit top of the Bundesliga right now, unbeaten in the league thus far, and with just one defeat all season in all competitions. That did come in the Champions League, away to Bodo Glimt, but this will be a tricky test tonight for Arsenal. Arteta says:.

I’m very impressed with them, you see the results so far, where they are in the Bundesliga at the top and where they are in the Champions League and especially the way they are playing, the way they are dominating games, the amount of threat they are able to create. We had them here in pre-season, and they demonstrated the quality and what they are capable of, so we are very much aware of that. But we play at home in front of our crowd, and now we’re going to go and attack the game, that’s for sure.

After a disappointing second half against Newcastle on Saturday, I’m sure the manager will be looking for a response from his side. It’s nice to be at home again, and a long spell of games in London will hopefully less taxing physically without all the travel, so it’d be good to get that off to a winning start tonight.

Elsewhere, Bruno Guimaraes spoke about his first few months at the club, and how he now feels like he’s getting to grips with what Mikel Arteta wants from him, saying:.

I’m here, I don’t know, three, four months? It’s still a lot to go, but I now definitely understand my role in the team, the way that Mikel wants me to play in the team. So, yeah, I think I still can play much, much better.

It has been revealed that and it’s quite interesting to hear him talk about how at Arsenal he is more ‘free’ than he was under Eddie Howe at Newcastle. Most would feel it was the other way around, but he explained:.

In a recent development, it’s very different. When I was at Newcastle, you play more positional, keep more your position. Here it’s a little bit more free.

If you see the game against Newcastle, they were marking us man to man. You see JT [Jurrien Timber] plays a six, an eight and a number nine sometimes, so you have to move a lot. Of course, I was not used to it. So now I understand a little bit more what he wants for the midfield.

Sources indicate that I think there’s more to come from him, he’s looked good at times, a little off the pace at others, and I think my main worry is about the physical side of his game. Does he have the running power and athleticism that enables players like Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard to thrive under this manager? At 29, he’s no spring chicken, but I guess there’s always room for improvement. Anyway, his press conference stuff from yesterday is worth reading, and there’s some good chat about him on the Arsecast Extra which you’ll find below.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. Don’t forget the updated Arseblog apps also have a cool new matchday centre, full of stats, alerts, and much more.

Industry News: Could Pep Guardiola succeed Thomas Tuchel as England manager after revealing his 'next step'?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 26 Nov 2026 16:12.
  • Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has confirmed that he wants to move into international management when he returns to football, an admission that raises an intriguing question about England's long-term aims beyond Thomas Tuchel's tenure.
  • The Spaniard has been taking a break from management since leaving the Etihad Stadium at the end of the 2025-26 season, bringing an end to a remarkable decade in which he won six Premier League titles and the Champions League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 26 Nov 2026 16:12.

Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has confirmed that he wants to move into international management when he returns to football, an admission that raises an intriguing question about England's long-term aims beyond Thomas Tuchel's tenure.

The Spaniard has been taking a break from management since leaving the Etihad Stadium at the end of the 2025-26 season, bringing an end to a remarkable decade in which he won six Premier League titles and the Champions League.

It has been revealed that although Guardiola has yet to establish a date for his return, the 55-year-old has a clear idea of what he wants to do next. His latest comments also shed light on how close he came to embarking on an international career last summer, when the Italian Football Federation approached him about taking charge of the Azzurri.

Speaking in an interview with his former Barcelona teammate Romario on Romario TV, Guardiola was asked whether there was a team he had never managed but would like to coach.

"A national team, which is my next step," replied the former Bayern Munich boss, who also explained that the timing of Italy's approach had prevented him from accepting the position.

"If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted," Guardiola admitted, explaining that his conversations with Paolo Maldini and Leonardo had taken place when he felt he needed a break from football.

Recent findings suggest that having spent 18 years in club management, Guardiola was reluctant to commit himself to another project so soon after leaving City. Italy subsequently appointed Roberto Mancini, while the Spaniard remains without a managerial position and has given no indication of when his sabbatical will end.

The United States are another potential destination following Mauricio Pochettino's departure to Manchester United. Guardiola has previously spoken enthusiastically about the potential of the American national team, although the prospect of managing England may also warrant consideration given the Football Association's reported interest in him in the past.

According to The Athletic, Guardiola was the FA's preferred candidate to replace Gareth Southgate following Euro 2024, with a verbal agreement reportedly in place before the Spaniard opted to remain at Manchester City.

His former Spain teammate Gaizka Mendieta has also identified England as a potential destination, alongside Brazil, believing that Guardiola would be attracted by the opportunity to compete for major international honours.

It has been revealed that england's current managerial situation could prove compatible with Guardiola's desire to take an extended break. Tuchel signed a contract extension in February to lead the Three Lions through to Euro 2028 and reiterated his commitment to that agreement earlier this month.

According to recent reports, the German, however, has also made no secret of his desire to return to club management once his England tenure comes to an end. Should he depart after the European Championship, his successor would have two years to prepare the national team for the 2030 World Cup.

It has been revealed that by that stage, Guardiola would have spent two seasons away from the dugout. The prospect of working with players such as Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice, Cole Palmer and Phil Foden would certainly be interesting from a tactical perspective, particularly given his preference for technically accomplished midfielders capable of operating in several positions.

His familiarity with English football and previous experience of working with several England internationals would also ease certain aspects of the transition, although implementing his demanding tactical approach within the limited training windows available to national team managers would represent a latest challenge.

There is presently nothing to suggest that the FA are looking beyond Tuchel or that Guardiola has identified England as his preferred destination. However, should the position become available in 2028, the circumstances could be considerably more favourable than when the FA reportedly approached him two years ago.

Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5198 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics.

Industry observers note that a, High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) image of the NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbon with Nb (3.4 nm) seed layer. The electrically-conducting width of this device is ~12.5 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed, together with their corresponding Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), obtained from the boxed regions in panel a. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions. In total, three NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbons were examined by cross-sectional STEM. Across these samples, we observe consistent structural and compositional characteristics, including similar NbP crystallinity and sidewall oxidation, which support the scaling behaviour reported in this work. Additional STEM characterization was not performed on thicker NbP nanoribbons, as the thinnest nanoribbons are most relevant to the main conclusions of this study.

a, HAADF image of the NbP (1.5 nm)/Nb (3.4 nm) nanoribbon with an electrically-conducting width of ~18 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed layer, together with their corresponding FFT, obtained from the boxed regions. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and EDS elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions of each region. e, EELS linescan profiles of Nb (blue) and P (red) normalized intensity as a function of position along the direction indicated in panel c. f-h, Representative nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data at probe positions within the sapphire substrate (f), Nb layer (g), and NbP layer (h), with indexed reflections confirming the distinct crystal structure of each region. i-k, Orientation template matching of the representative NBED pattern in f–h, for the sapphire substrate (i), Nb layer (j) and NbP layer (k). Coloured symbols indicate the local crystallographic orientation of the best-matching template for that pattern. l-n, Phase template matching of the same patterns for the sapphire substrate (l), Nb layer (m) and NbP layer (n).

a, Schematic of the scaling mechanism for conventional metals, with surface scattering and grain boundary scattering. b, As thickness and width of NbP are reduced, the conduction is consistent with the growing dominance of surface carriers, which are disorder-tolerant, with reduced scattering. The total sheet conductance in this case is a sum of the sheet conductance contributed from bulk carriers and surface carriers. c, For thick NbP, bulk carriers dominate the transport, and thus conventional scaling laws apply, with pronounced surface and grain boundary scattering. d, The Fuchs-Sondheimer (FS) and Mayadas-Shatzkes (MS) model fitting of 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, showing an excellent fit. The extracted resistivity with increasing width (W → ∞) is 56.3 μΩ∙cm, which matches the literature results. e, Sheet conductance (GNbP,□) of 1.5 nm NbP as a function of width (red curve), extracted from Fig. 2d of the main text. The sheet conductance from bulk carriers (extracted from Hall measurement) follows the conventional FS-MS scaling model (black dashed line), where the sheet conductance from surface carriers increases as the width decreases due to the increased surface area/volume ratio, as indicated by the purple dashed line. At this ultrathin thickness (1.5 nm), bulk carriers experience strong scattering, resulting in very small bulk carrier sheet conductance. f, GNbP,□ of 10 nm NbP as a function of width (blue curve). At NbP thickness of 10 nm, 3D bulk carriers and 2D top and bottom surface carriers contribute comparably to transport, as shown in Fig. 4b. At this thickness, as the nanoribbon width is reduced, the enhancement in surface conduction is insufficient to offset the increased scattering of bulk carriers. Consequently, bulk transport dominates in this regime, leading to a net reduction of sheet conductance (i.e., increased resistivity) with decreasing width, more similar to conventional metal wires. We note that there could be subtle differences in sidewall roughness and damage in the thicker nanoribbons compared to the thinner ones. See Supplementary Note 2 for the modelling details and more discussion.

It has been revealed that a, Bulk Brillouin-zone schematic showing the two mirror planes and nodal rings from the band inversion. b, Representative band dispersion along Γ-S-M’, where the curves calculated without spin-orbit coupling (SOC) show the nodal-ring-related band inversion (plotted in green), and the curves calculated with SOC show the corresponding gap opening (black dashed lines). c, Real-space crystal view highlighting the helical states along the projected mirror line on the surface. d, Surface-state spectrum along \(\overline{\Gamma }\)-\(\overline{{\rm{X}}}\)-\(\overline{\Gamma }\)’, where the narrow Weyl-point window (grey shadow) hosts three pairs of helical states (indicated by arrows) that form the main part of the Fermi arcs, while remnant spin-split surface branches remain visible over a broader energy window (broad green shadow). Blue and red colours indicate the ‘± Sy’ spin polarization at opposite momenta, showing the helical feature. In summary, the narrow Fermi-arc structure is embedded inside a much broader nodal-ring-derived surface-state sector set by the band inversion. See Supplementary Note 7 for more discussion on bulk-topology hierarchy and topological surface-state interpretation.

Recent findings suggest that a, Slab model along the [001] direction for the surface state calculations. Here, the 2 × 2 × 3 supercell is shown as an example. A 4.5 nm thick slab structure of the 1 × 1 × 4 supercell was used in the calculations. b,c, Surface band structures with Nb (b) and P (c) terminations along high-symmetry lines. Blue and red bands indicate the surface states of the Nb and P terminations, respectively. Bulk-projected states shown in pale blue are depicted as the background. The charge neutral point is set to 0 eV. d-f, Surface-projected Fermi surfaces with Nb (upper panels) and P (lower panels) terminations at 0 eV (d), −0.2 eV (e), and −0.4 eV (f). Darker colours represent larger contributions projected from the surface. Weyl points projected on the 2D Brillouin zone are shown as green and purple dots for opposite chirality. The constant energy cuts show surface-dominant open contours over a broad energy window, indicating that Weyl-derived surface bands persist even when the chemical potential is shifted deep into the hole-doped regime, which implies the robustness of the topological surface character. In addition, for the 4.5 nm thick NbP film, the top and bottom surface states exhibit minimal hybridization, except near the Weyl point projections where they meet each other. The Fermi-arc states remain largely unhybridized because they are well separated in momentum space. Even at momenta where they intersect, the resulting hybridization gap is negligible. See Supplementary Note 8 for the modelling details and more discussion.

a, Slab model from the NbP (001) film with thickness d = 1.5 nm and width W = 4.4 to 5.7 nm. b, The one-dimensional (1D) band structure of a W = 5 nm nanoribbon along ky direction. The edge projection is highlighted in purple to show the edge states, while the bulk states are shown in pale blue. Near EF, the edge-projected subbands form an electron-like pocket, consistent with the negative pedge values (panel f). c-e, The spin projection to Sx (c), Sy (d), and Sz (e) components, respectively, for the edge state. The blue and red represent opposite signs of spin polarization. These edge states exhibit a pronounced spin texture arising from strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in noncentrosymmetric NbP where Sx and Sz components are locked to the ky momentum in a Rashba-type SOC. This reduces the wavefunction overlap between counter-propagating modes, thereby suppressing the leading backscattering channel, which indicates high-mobility edge conduction. f, The carrier densities from edge (pedge) and 2D film (p2D) are extracted from linear fitting of the total ribbon density (p1D) by p1D = pedge + p2DW, at varying W. Wc denotes the cross-over width at which the edge carrier density would dominate the transport over the top and bottom surface carrier density. Here, Wc ≈ 0 indicates that the enhanced edge conduction of ultrathin films is not primarily driven by an increased edge carrier density. Instead, it is more plausibly attributed to an enhanced carrier mobility arising from reduced backscattering as the edge dimension approaches the quasi-1D limit. See more details in Supplementary Notes 2 and 8. g, Agreement between the nanoribbon fitting (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{NR}}}\)) and that obtained from independent slab film calculations (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{slab}}}\)) which corresponds to the d = 1.5 nm thickness in Supplementary Fig. 10. This agreement supports the self-consistency of our calculations across both the nanoribbon and thin-film geometries.

a, Temperature-dependent effective resistivity (ρeff) of NbP films with different thicknesses up to 90 nm, measured from Hall bar devices. These films have a 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, whose resistivity is measured separately (black symbols). b, Low-temperature limit (2-10 K) of panel a. The smallest superconducting transition temperature Tc (~2.2 K) is in the 3.4 nm Nb layer (black symbols), while higher Tc are observed in the NbP/Nb films, and Tc decreases monotonically with thicker NbP. The symbol colours follow the convention in panel a. c,d, Temperature-dependent sheet conductance (GNbP,□) (c) and resistivity (ρNbP) (d) for all NbP thicknesses, after subtracting the Nb seed contribution. e, ρNbP as a function of NbP thickness at 300 K and 10 K. For comparison, the ρNbP values of nanoribbons with the widest widths (Fig. 2d of the main text) are slightly higher than those from Hall measurements at 300 K, possibly due to process-induced damage during nanofabrication. f, Temperature-dependent ρeff of a ~5 nm-thick Nb control film, measured from a Hall bar device. The residual resistivity ratio (RRR) is 1.48, and the Tc is ~4.2 K. Inset: enlarged view of the low-temperature region. The presence of NbP appears to promote superconductivity in NbP/Nb films. The superconducting proximity effect is one plausible interpretation, although changes in disorder and enhanced inter-grain coupling (in the presence of NbP layer) could also contribute. We also cannot fully rule out the formation of an interfacial superconducting layer at the NbP/Nb interface. The NbP sheet conductance is obtained by subtracting the sheet conductance of the Nb layer (measured independently on control Nb films) from the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack. The extracted NbP resistivity is then obtained by dividing the NbP thickness by the NbP sheet conductance, i.e. ρNbP = dNbP/GNbP,□, where GNbP,□ = Gtot,□ - GNb,□ and Gtot,□ = dtot/ρeff, where Gtot,□ is the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack, dtot is the total stack thickness and ρeff is the measured effective resistivity (panel a). The GNbP,□ (panel c) represents the NbP sheet conductance after subtracting the independently-measured Nb seed contribution. Additional validation of the subtraction method using Pt/Nb stacks is provided in Supplementary Fig. 19. Control experiments using Pt/Nb stacks validate that the subtraction procedure itself does not generate an anomalous resistivity trend. Nevertheless, the conductance of the Nb seed layer within NbP/Nb stacks cannot be independently measured and it cannot be mentioned, with absolute certainty, that its behaviour is identical to that of the separately measured Nb control film. Thus, the extracted NbP resistivity relies, by necessity, on the model used.

a-c, Hall resistance (Rxy) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for 3.4 nm Nb (a), 1.5 nm NbP (b), and 10 nm NbP (c). For the NbP films (b,c), the Nb seed layer contribution is subtracted at each corresponding temperature to extract NbP Hall response, using the same two-layer Hall conduction model described in the supplement. d, Effective three-dimensional carrier density (p3D) for all films, revealing opposite temperature-dependence: ultrathin 1.5 nm NbP indicates an increasing p3D upon cooling, whereas both thicker NbP (10 nm) and Nb (3.4 nm) display decreasing p3D. (This figure is also included in the main text as Fig. 4d and is reproduced here for convenience). e, Effective hole mobility (μp) of the same films vs. temperature. NbP films exhibit a pronounced increase in mobility upon cooling due to suppressed phonon scattering, whereas the 3.4 nm Nb film shows only a slight rise in mobility, indicating that its transport remains strongly limited by surface scattering.

a-c, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for films of Nb seed layer (3.4 nm) (a), for NbP (1.5 nm) on the Nb seed (b), and for NbP (10 nm) on the Nb seed (c). All measurements were performed with the magnetic field applied perpendicular to the film plane and current direction. At low temperatures, all films exhibit a pronounced negative cusp near low field regions, arising from the interplay of superconducting fluctuations and weak antilocalization. d-e, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at 1.8 K for both 1.5 nm thick NbP (on 3.4 nm Nb seed layer) and for the Nb layer (3.4 nm) evaluated separately. Measurements were performed with B field perpendicular to the film plane and current direction (d), and with B applied in-plane (e). The superconducting transition temperatures are Tc ~ 6 K for the 1.5 nm NbP (on Nb) and ~2.2 K for the 3.4 nm Nb film (see Fig. 3d of the main text). The upper critical field Hc2, defined as the midpoint between the normal state resistance and zero resistance, is extracted. At 1.8 K, the out-of-plane critical field \({H}_{c2}^{\perp }\) is 2.2 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and 0.38 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The in-plane critical field at 1.8 K exceeds 9 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and reaches 4.44 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The superconducting coherence length estimates are provided in the supplement. The sense current used for Hall bar measurements is 0.5 mA, corresponding to a current density of ~0.1 MA/cm2 for the NbP (1.5 nm) film and ~0.15 MA/cm2 for the 3.4 nm Nb control, with the same 100 μm Hall bar device width. We note that this sense current is well below the superconducting critical current: even when we increased the sense current up to 10 mA, we were unable to suppress the superconducting state at 1.8 K.

a, Cross-sectional HAADF STEM image of the alternating NbP/Nb multilayers grown on sapphire. b-d, Denoised nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data for all Nb layers (Nb layers 1-3) showing consistent body-centred cubic (bcc) diffraction symmetry with indexed reflections, confirming crystalline quality across all Nb layers. Scale bars: 0.5 Å−1. e, EDS line scan across the multilayer stack showing Nb (blue), P (red), and Al (light brown) as a function of position, integrated over a ~ 5nm wide region along the direction indicated by the yellow arrow in panel a, confirming periodic composition and abrupt elemental transitions at each NbP/Nb interface. f-h, denoised NBED patterns from NbP layers 1–3, displaying diffraction symmetry consistent with the NbP crystal structure with indexed reflections, consistent with uniform phase and crystallographic orientation throughout the multilayer stack. The diffraction spots become progressively broader from layer 1 to layer 3, suggesting a gradual decrease in crystalline coherence in NbP layers further from the substrate. This is further supported by the emergence of diffuse ring features in the Layer 3 diffraction pattern, indicative of increasing structural disorder.

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has named his starting line-up for tonight’s crucial Europa League game away against Olympiacos.

It has been revealed that milan have lost three of their opening four games in the competition and they are running out of runway to put things right. With 12 points up for grabs, the feeling is that the Rossoneri need at least a couple of wins to even get a play-off spot, given they sit outside the top 24 at present.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

They face an Olympiacos side that have 10 points on the board already thanks to three wins and a draw, while they have conceded only once. Not helping matters for Amorim is the fact that there are nine absentees due to injury.

On paper, Milan will line up with a four-man defence of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Pervis Estupinan in front of the goalkeeper and captain Mike Maignan. Davide Bartesaghi was the latest injury, making the change at left-back a forced one.

According to recent reports, luka Modric’s muscle strain means that Ardon Jashari will get another chance in the double pivot, alongside Adrien Rabiot who will play a bit deeper tonight. Omari Hutchinson, Alphadjo Cisse and Diego Moreira will then the centre-forward Goncalo Ramos in a 4-2-3-1 formation.

Matteo Pittarella, Valeri Vladimirov, Christian Comotto and Lorenzo Ossola all feature on a youthful bench, as well as Christian Pulisic and usual starting midfielder Yunus Musah.

Official Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupiñán; Jashari, Rabiot; Hutchinson, Cisse, Moreira; Ramos.

Bench: Pittarella, Torriani, Tomori, Comotto, V. Vladimirov, Ossola, Terracciano, Musah, Pulisic.

Official Olympiacos XI (4-2-3-1):Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Pirola, Bruno; Freuler Gustavo Sà; Gelson Martins, Jota Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

Bench: Stournaras, Georgakopoulos, Saliakas, David Carmo, Fortounis, Yaremchuk, Bakoulas, Tiknizyan, Filis, Toufakis.

Man Utd transfer news: Barca 'reach decision' on selling Bruno Fernandes successor to Red Devils

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 16:19.

Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea have reportedly suffered a major blow in their pursuits of Barcelona star Fermin Lopez.

Mauricio Pochettino's Red Devils are currently occupying 19th position in the Premier League standings after their worst-ever start to the competition, picking up just the single top-flight victory to date.

Following a defeat by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, Man Utd managed to record a 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night, when the visitors were arguably unlucky to miss out on maximum points.

On the fringes of Michael Carrick's and now Pochettino's prepares at Old Trafford, Marcus Rashford could supposedly move away from the club during the January transfer window if a suitable offer arrives.

Elsewhere in attack, Bruno Fernandes has been the club's best player since the start of the decade, however, the Portugal international could be on his way out of Man Utd next summer.

According to TEAMtalk, Premier League giants Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea all made enquiries for Barcelona's Lopez during the recent summer transfer window, with the Spanish side snubbing those advances.

The 23-year-old put pen to paper on a fresh deal at the beginning of this calendar year and it is understood that the attacker has commenced talks with the Catalan club over another contract extension.

With the player's current deal expiring in June 2031, Barca are in no danger of losing Lopez on the cheap anytime soon, however, Hansi Flick's side are keen to reward the Spaniard further for an exceptional start to the 2026-27 campaign.

The former Linares Deportivo loanee has become such an integral figure at Camp Nou that the interested Premier League trio have supposedly been told to 'forget about' their dreams of signing the forward.

The future of Fernandes at Man Utd is unclear heading towards his contract expiration in June, with the Red Devils reportedly highlighting Barca's Lopez as a potential successor to the Portuguese's Old Trafford spot.

Yet to reach top form, Lopez was not a guaranteed starter for Flick's Barcelona last season - a situation that allowed Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea to dream of signing the talent.

However, the picture surrounding the 23-year-old has changed dramatically this campaign, with the 12-time international starting 10 La Liga matches already, cementing a spot in the XI behind the lone striker.

In all competitions, Lopez has netted nine times and provided seven assists across 17 appearances, with only Lamine Yamal and Raphinha notching up more goal contributions for Barca in La Liga.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that the rulings came in Official Communiqué No.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

It has been revealed that juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

It has been revealed that the rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

That leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

Sources indicate that it ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

It has been revealed that the count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

#129129. Arsenal 1-1 Dortmund: Familiar flaws hold Arsenal back

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1733 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arseblog ↗ Open Full Page

Arsenal 1-1 Dortmund: Familiar flaws hold Arsenal back

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1733 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday raised some very familiar concerns and, if we’re being honest, revealed nothing we didn’t already know.
  • Sources indicate that arsenal can play world-class football and completely dominate teams for long spells, but lack the world-class attack to make the most of that domination, the sort of players you just know will create and convert big chances when the time comes.
  • According to recent reports, I really feel like I could write two versions of today’s blog.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday raised some very familiar concerns and, if we’re being honest, revealed nothing we didn’t already know.

Sources indicate that arsenal can play world-class football and completely dominate teams for long spells, but lack the world-class attack to make the most of that domination, the sort of players you just know will create and convert big chances when the time comes. And the way the team is starting games after the break is worrying, with teams who are battered to within an inch of their lives early on suddenly able to compete.

According to recent reports, I really feel like I could write two versions of today’s blog. One where I’m miserable, of course: the players can’t shoot, they make all the wrong choices in the decisive moment, we can’t keep wasting chances and dropping off after the break, if Andrea Berta doesn’t deliver the true heirs to Thierry Henry and Robert Pires in January, then he should be stuffed into one of the cannons outside the Armoury and fired into the cold night air.

The other version is much more glass half full: Arteta is coaching masterclasses every week, this level of dominance in games is something I could only dream of a few years ago, that’s the most shots we’ve had in a game all season, we’re top of the league, we’re creating loads without any set-piece reliance and without Bukayo Saka – the goals will come.

It has been revealed that some people reading this would prefer (and relate better to) one version, and others the other version, I’m sure. Let’s see where we end up!

Sources indicate that there were, as there tends to be in these Champions League games, a fair few changes from the weekend. Kepa, Piero Hincapie, Ben White, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis, and Viktor Gyokeres all came into the team.

Despite featuring half a different side, there were plenty of parallels with the Newcastle match. Arsenal were dominant from the off, with Hincapie and White taking turns to play off of Gyokeres. Dortmund had no idea how to cover them and both fullbacks were the targets of early crosses into the box.

In a recent development, after a couple of long-range efforts, Arsenal got their goal they deserved, with Gyokeres launching a ferocious, dipping effort beyond Gregor Kobel. The Swede can put his foot through the ball, that’s for sure, and the Dortmund backline gave him the sort of time and space to set himself that he doesn’t often get.

The pressure continued after the opener for a while, with Tzolis forcing a good save and Madueke just unable to sort his feet to tap in the rebound.

It’s fair to say the game settled down after 15/20 minutes, with Dortmund growing into it a little, but it was still Arsenal who looked like scoring the next goal. Rice shot over from almost the same patch of grass Gyokeres had scored from, and the midfielder had another chance when a beautiful one-touch move ended with him bursting through, hurtling towards the Dortmund box. Maybe he could’ve picked out Madueke in support, but he went alone and Nico Schlotterbeck just got across to block the shot.

It has been revealed that another huge chance was denied by the offside flag as much as the finishing – Madueke won the ball high, Odegaard squared it to Gyokeres, and the Swede fired over from near the penalty spot. Odegaard was ruled offside but I’m not convinced: had the ball hit the net, I think we’d have seen a very tight VAR check.

Sources indicate that there was one thought on everyone’s minds at half-time: don’t do the same thing again. After Slavia Prague and Newcastle, do not do the same thing again.

Arsenal did the same thing again.

There was an early warning sign with Dortmund sliding the ball across the box and Maximilian Beier kicking the air. He didn’t make the same mistake with his next opportunity. Centre-back Joane Gadou (who was very impressive all evening) charged through the heart of the pitch before playing the ball to Beier, who jinked to unbalance Gabriel and slotted home.

Industry observers note that sometimes a goal is just a good goal, and I don’t think anyone was really at fault here. It’s a great run from Gadou, Beier tricks Gabriel to take the ball onto his weaker left side – it’s fair if Gabriel is expecting (and blocking the angle) on the attacker’s favoured foot, I know how that can happen. I think if we score that goal we’re talking about two brilliant individuals, rather than defensive errors.

Sources indicate that my first thought? Not again. My second? OK, how do we respond? Because on Saturday, the response was poor.

It has been revealed that this time it was a lot better. Jobe Bellingham had a rebound disallowed for offside, a moment that really brought the crowd back into the game, but in truth, that was Dortmund’s only real moment of threat. From the goal on 55 minutes to full-time, Arsenal had 15 shots to Dortmund’s two.

And that doesn’t include Serhou Guirassy playing one-twos with the post after a clever, low free-kick from Martin Odegaard late on.

Madueke had an effort blocked. Gyokeres flicked a header wide. Madueke shot wide beyond the far post after a good run. Gyokeres missed a big chance with his head from six yards out. Rice hit the near post from a tight angle after a brilliant pass from Eberechi Eze.

A couple of late corners came to nothing, and that was it.

Mikel Arteta was clearly pleased with the performance on the whole:.

Well, I think I love the way the team played. There’s no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were, how connected everybody was to the game … It was great to watch. It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball hasn’t ended up in the back of the net. That’s my feeling.

to do what we’ve done out there is just something to be very, very pleased about, because there is very little more that we can demand from the team.

But we all know what that little more is:.

Sources indicate that obviously the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance, the amount of chances, the situation, and even shots that are not there. We are three against two, two against one, and the ball doesn’t land with the right person. There is an element of luck, there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist, because I think what the team has done and shown today is the right direction.

It has been revealed that often when Arsenal don’t win games, it feels like it’s because the team haven’t created enough chances. We end up focusing on that one moment, where that one player didn’t execute the way you wanted. But last night wasn’t one of those: Arsenal didn’t struggle to turn dominance into good, slick football, and that football into a healthy number of decent opportunities.

Recent findings suggest that that’s incredibly frustrating, but I do think you win a lot more often than not when you do that. Maybe that’s a hard sell for some this morning, but it’s how I feel about it when we play well, especially when we’ve been winning games anyway. That’s the first time this season we’ve gone two without a win across all competitions, and we’ve won 14 of 19 games so far. Sometimes things don’t fall for you, and this one felt a lot like ‘one of those’, certainly more than Newcastle did.

A word for a couple of promising performances too, with the boss asked about Gyokeres in his post-match press conference:.

Industry observers note that what I love the most is how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways. His link-up play, the way he held the ball, the way he threw it in behind and stretched the pitch. There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s the victory that we need.

Recent findings suggest that his finishing was off after the brilliant opener, but at least he was in the positions: too often this season and last, Gyokeres has gone through a game barely registering a shot. He had seven last night, and if he can do that more often he’ll score a lot more. His general play was improved too, both holding the ball up and competing in behind.

In a recent development, and I thought Martin Odegaard was excellent too. His eight chances created from open play was the most of any player in any Champions League match so far this season.

Industry observers note that since we returned to the competition in 2023, we’ve had a player create more than five chances in a match just twice: Odegaard at Napoli in September (6) and Odegaard last night (9). He’s incredibly unlucky not to be leaving the game with a couple of assists.

In a recent development, the draw leaves us in a decent position to finish in the all-important top eight in the league phase still, although you have to squint a bit to see us landing in the also-important top two. Real Madrid are up next and that’s a reminder of the sort of teams we’re up against: finishing in the top two is a tall order at the best of times.

According to recent reports, with each passing game, it is impossible not to wonder what could be done in January to add to the team. Unless there’s a sudden uptick out of nowhere, those thoughts aren’t disappearing. And even if there is a massive uptick, those thoughts will still be around. But 30 shots is the most we’ve had in a game all season, and the same group of players have scored more goals with fewer shots (/chances) plenty of times. Let’s hope we see some more clinical finishing on Sunday.

Guess I landed on the glass half full version.

It has been revealed that there should be an Arsecast once Blogs has caught up with the game, so stay tuned for that. Enjoy your Wednesdays!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alisson is one of Liverpool's biggest-named players to be linked with an exit this summer.

The Brazilian's contract is set to expire in June 2027 and, right now, it doesn't feel like the Reds are going to offer him a new deal.

Indeed, rumours about both ends of the deal have been emerging and, even though the former Roma man has been an important asset for Liverpool this term, his age coupled with the sheer number of goalkeepers the Reds have on their books make a deal difficult.

Obviously, Alisson's time at the club has been well regarded. He's won two Premier League titles and one Champions League trophy.

But, since he's now in the twilight stages of his career, Liverpool need to approach this deal with caution and weigh up their options before making a final decision.

Lucas Chevalier wants to leave Paris Saint-Germain, Liverpool could make a move.

Having a decent goalkeeper is one of the most vital things for any football team.

Even if you have one of the best teams in the world in terms of outfielders, if your goalkeeper is poor, they're more than likely going to let you down.

This was the case when Giorgi Mamardashvili played last season with fans demanding that a latest 'keeper was signed.

Initially, the Georgian was expected to take over from the Brazilian but, thanks to how poorly he performed, that didn't end up being the case.

Mamardashvili's poor form led to fans wondering who their next goalkeeper could be with a fresh update from L'Equipe now making that more than clear.

Sources indicate that "Lucas Chevalier is ready to leave Paris Saint-Germain this winter. But there are many conditions for a departure. PSG will notably have to find a replacement before considering letting him go," they wrote.

Lucas Chevalier would be an out of the box signing for Liverpool.

When Chevalier was brought to PSG by Luis Enrique, fans, pundits and journalists all thought that the Frenchman was destined to become their first choice.

Obviously he had some major shoes to fill after Gianluigi Donnarumma exited for Manchester City but, for Enrique's style of play, the Frenchman was the better option.

But, for one reason or another, the 25-year-old didn't hit the right notes and has been downgraded to their back-up by Matvey Safonov.

Neither of them are considered among the world's best but, Chevalier is almost certainly a better option for Liverpool than Mamardashvili would be.

Others such as Bart Verbruggen and Diogo Costa have also been linked with Liverpool but, since Chevalier actually wants to exit, a deal for him might be easier for Liverpool to agree on with PSG.

Nobody knows what the future has in store for any of Liverpool's first team squad but, if Chevalier is a player welcomed through the Anfield doors, the Reds will be in a decent place, even if he is replacing Alisson.

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 16:24.

Motherwell and Hibernian will come together on Saturday evening for a Scottish Premiership clash at Fir Park.

The hosts are 11th in the Scottish Premiership table with 13 points, while the visitors are ninth with 14 points.

Motherwell initially recorded a positive start to the 2026-27 Scottish Premiership season, winning two and drawing two of their first four league games under new boss Alfred Johansson.

However, the Steelmen have subsequently recorded just one win in the following 10 league fixtures, alongside two draws and seven defeats.

That run included a particularly miserable six-game losing streak from September 5 to October 25, which was eventually ended by two draws and a win at the end of October and early November.

However, another defeat last weekend, a 2-1 loss to Rangers, has culminated in Motherwell falling to 11th in the standings with just 13 points from 14 games, leaving Johansson under increasing pressure.

Motherwell's biggest issue this term has been their lack of goals, with just 16 scored in 14 league games, although they have managed to find the back of the net in each of their last four matches.

Desperate to avoid slipping further away from safety and closer to the bottom, especially with 12th-placed Kilmarnock taking on 10th-placed St Mirren, Motherwell will be eager to pick up just their fourth league win of the season on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Hibernian head into Saturday's matchday 15 encounter in resurgent form, having won three, drawn one and lost just one of their last five games across all competitions.

The first of those triumphs saw Hibernian come from behind to defeat rivals Hearts 2-1 in the Scottish League Cup semi-final, securing their place in the final and marking Marink Reedijk's first win as manager.

The subsequent two victories, 4-0 against Aberdeen and 2-1 against Dundee, have both come in the league, helping Hibernian climb out of the relegation zone and into ninth place.

Hibernian will be looking to build on that improved form with another victory on Saturday, especially as they aim to continue climbing up the table - at the moment trailing sixth-placed St Johnstone by just three points.

Alongside their recent run, Hibs will draw further confidence from their strength on the road this season, picking up 10 of their 14 points when playing away from home.

Fat margins

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1019 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that thanks to Lewis for taking care of the blog yesterday as I was unable to watch the Borussia Dortmund match live.
  • I think while I have some frustrations overall with our inability to turn dominance into goals, I’m more comfortable with it when we’re actually making chances.
  • It wasn’t that long ago that it was the other way around.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that thanks to Lewis for taking care of the blog yesterday as I was unable to watch the Borussia Dortmund match live. I saw that we’d scored early but only saw the final score well after the full-time whistle, so I guess it was a little disappointing not to have built on that fantastic hit from Viktor Gyokeres.

I think while I have some frustrations overall with our inability to turn dominance into goals, I’m more comfortable with it when we’re actually making chances. I think the manager would have a far bigger glitch on his hands if we weren’t, and on Tuesday night the fact we had 30 attempts on goal tells you the problem isn’t chance creation, it’s about being clinical.

It wasn’t that long ago that it was the other way around. We found it hard to make goalscoring opportunities and for me that’s much more of a worry. It doesn’t mean we can’t improve, it doesn’t mean January becomes any less notable the closer it gets, it’s just that the solution lies with the players we have who should be capable of better. There were a couple of other opportunities for Gyokeres that could easily have made this a better night for him and for Arsenal, Declan Rice hit the post, fine margins that shouldn’t be impossible to squeeze in our favour. Make ’em wider, thicker.

In the end though, I think the bottom line is quality of personnel. Over the last few seasons the only front three player we’ve had who looked like he could become top, top quality was Bukayo Saka. He was certainly on that trajectory until injuries became a real hindrance, and we saw that this season there were modifications made to his game to make him more effective. I know the discourse around him was a little polarised, but I saw a player more involved, who looked sharper and capable of producing the kind of volume that made him so impactful.

According to recent reports, saka isn’t one of those who finishes every chance he gets, he’s a guy who just keeps going until he makes something happen. The hamstring injury, and then the ongoing Achilles matter made it harder for him to contribute, but I really was encouraged by his season until the injury he sustained against Bayern. And it’s interesting to me that while it might be the kind of player he is anyway, we’ve basically asked Noni Madueke to replicate ‘Old Saka’ in terms of that kind of volume of shots and crosses. He’s had 11 shots across the last two games, and perhaps a single goal from those appear to be a scant return, I think it’s how we need him to play and how Arsenal can maximise what we’ve got up front.

There was an interesting comment on the Arses yesterday wondering how it is that Mikel Arteta can coach and improve defenders and midfielders so well, but not do the same with his attacking players. Some will say it’s because he’s a coach who is defensively minded and this is his wheelhouse. This is what he’s good at. Make a great defence, build a solid midfield in front of them. Perhaps there’s an element of truth in that, but for me it’s down to the players he has to work with.

If the raw ingredients are good, the recipe has a much better chance of being good, regardless of the talent of the chef. If you get to work with players like Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard etc, all of whom arrived in at a relatively young age (Rice perhaps the exception because he had a lot of experience, but Arteta has still made him better), you can develop that potential, build relationships, and see that come to fruition on the pitch.

Up front though, I don’t think we’ve had that level of talent. What can you do with a Willian or a Marquinhos? What can you do with a Gabriel Jesus whose knee explodes (perhaps as we saw in those opening few months before injury hit, you could have done a lot more)? Was Gabriel Martinelli’s plateau down to Arteta’s coaching or the player’s ceiling? I think the fact he’s playing now in Saudi Arabia notes a bit about that. I think Arteta squeezed a lot out of someone like Leandro Trossard, who arrived at 28 and became a better player than he was at Brighton, but ultimately there are limits. The same goes for our two strikers, Gyokeres and Kai Havertz. On their days, they can get you goals, but there are too many days when they won’t, and I don’t really think it’s a coaching issue.

We also need to remember that there was a season when Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal scored more goals than the Invincibles did when they won the league in 2004. It’s not as if his coaching, per se, is an impediment to scoring goals – but like anything it’s layered and multi-factored. We had to become more defensive when all of our attackers were basically banjaxed, we still managed to finish second that season when all we had on the bench was a end-stage Raheem Sterling. If that has tipped the balance a little too far the other way, then you can understand it, and Arsenal are the masters of the single-goal margin victory these days.

Recent findings suggest that I think we can do more to score more, I think some of the players we have are capable of delivering more goals and assists, and over the next few months – being realistic about what we might do in January – that’s what we need to lean into. But my gut feeling is that until such time as we have better attackers to work with, this will remain an issue – and it’s worth saying that said issue is one we still find a way to achieve success with more often than that.

I’d just like some fat margins once in a while.

In a recent development, defenders Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo hurt their hamstrings at Napoli, leaving unbeaten Serie A leaders Lazio short in defence. The setback hits Gattuso's back line just as Juventus return from the break chasing the leaders.

Lazio’s defence has suffered a double blow. Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo were both injured in the 1-1 draw at Napoli. The timing is awkward for the leaders, who resume their league campaign against Lecce on 21 November.

Exact recovery times will only be set once all clinical tests are complete. The early estimate is about 20 days for each player, Sky Sport Italia reported. On that timeline, both miss the home game against Lecce and could return for the trip to Torino on 28 November.

Not every report is that hopeful. Football Italia reported that the pair should miss both the Lecce and Torino games. Under that scenario, they hope to be available again in the first week of December. The match against Atalanta on 6 December is also in doubt.

Recent findings suggest that tavares has been a real attacking outlet this season. He has one goal and four assists in 11 Serie A games. He also has a long record of muscle injuries. Sutalo has made eight league appearances since joining on loan from Ajax on 22 August.

Lazio must now turn to their alternatives. Alfonso Pedraza, who joined from Villarreal in the summer, is the leading option at left-back. He has played 322 minutes across the league and Coppa Italia. Diogo Leite and Doekhi are competing to replace Sutalo in the middle.

The stand-ins inherit a strong record. Lazio have scored 25 goals and conceded 9 so far. Keeping that defensive record with a reshuffled back line is now Gattuso’s task.

Juventus know Lazio’s quality first-hand. Gattuso’s side won 3-0 in Turin earlier this season. That result still weighs on the table. Five wins, three draws and three defeats make up the Juventus record from their opening games.

Grande chiusura di Sutalo, fondamentale.

— S.S.Lazio (@OfficialSSLazio) November 8, 2026.

Two missing defenders will not close the gap on their own. They do, however, give Juventus a window in which the leaders are weaker than usual. Any dropped points by Lazio over the coming rounds would only count if Juventus take care of their own fixtures.

According to recent reports, those fixtures follow Lazio’s closely. Como v Juventus is scheduled for Sunday 29 November at 20:45, the day after Lazio’s game against Torino. Further ahead, Lazio’s aim is to have both defenders fit for the Rome derby on 13 December.
