Khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures. Højbjerg has emerged as the name Juventus want to cover the gap in January.

It has been revealed that two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures. Thuram should be back with the group in January, and Locatelli only in the spring, Sport Mediaset reported. Both men are recovering from operations on the right knee.

Sources indicate that thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the procedure at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon. Locatelli had his external meniscus sutured, also in Lyon, after spraining the knee against Milan. He was due to start rehabilitation the day after the operation.

Spalletti now has to rely on Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and newly introduced signing Pape Matar Sarr in the middle. The run opens with Venezia at 12:30 on 22 November. Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Sources indicate that como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

In a recent development, the table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

It has been revealed that the absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

In a recent development, the profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

Sources indicate that until then, the existing group must carry the load. The Coppa Italia tie with Sassuolo is set for the Allianz Stadium in Turin on Thursday 3 December at 21:00.

Industry observers note that liverpool have a new star. One player has officially revealed himself as a key player with a fantastic performance.

Liverpool went into this season with a very imbalanced squad. It was one that required a lot from new head coach Andoni Iraola, essentially asking him to improve and experiment with players to get the most out of it.

Sources indicate that of course, that's largely the job of a head coach but it's rare that so much experimentation was necessary from a UEFA Champions League side that won the Premier League two seasons ago. But that's what Liverpool offered Iraola after two transfer windows that tore up large portions of the team.

No defensive midfielders, no recognised right-back, four left-wingers, no right-wingers, and one fit centre-forward. Hardly a 'win now' group of players. Iraola, though, has worked some real magic.

According to recent reports, and that includes solving the defensive midfielder problem. At least for now.

The midfielder problem was a surprise one. We fully expected Liverpool to invest in the middle of the pitch over the summer but they simply ignored the matter. Even more bizarre was a decision to sell Curtis Jones without any sort of replacement.

It left Iraola short but it's a problem he appears to have fixed. Trey Nyoni has stepped up incredibly well, moving from a mere youth player who hoped for minutes to a genuine starting threat in the span of just a few months.

According to recent reports, wednesday night, though, felt like an announcement of sorts. Nyoni started away from home in the UEFA Champions League and thrived, holding down the midfield against a rampant Club Brugge.

Sources indicate that liverpool’s clean sheet made them the first team to hold out against Brugge for a very, very long time. The first team to beat Brugge in months, too.

According to recent reports, nyoni played his part. He wasn’t necessarily a defensive force by the way he won tackles here, it was more about his efforts on the ball to keep Liverpool ticking over.

According to recent reports, 92 per cent pass completion away from home in the Champions League is fantastic. It’s even more fantastic that he did it while completing 11 line-breaking passes - this wasn’t a case of Nyoni simply picking the simple ball every time.

That 11 was the third-highest figure in the match and second-highest for Liverpool (Jeremy Jacquet had 13). It’s exactly the kind of midfield play that the Reds have been crying out for and doing it at a difficult ground in the premiere competition is just outstanding from a 19-year-old.

Nyoni is special and this felt like an announcement. Confirmation that he is a proper star player and one Liverpool can count on in major fixtures.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 26 Nov 2026 16:40, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 16:42.

An vital game at the bottom end of the League One table will take place at the Cherry Red Records Stadium on Saturday, as AFC Wimbledon welcome Barnsley.

The hosts sit 18th but only lead the drop zone by three points while their visitors are rooted to the foot of the division and in the midst of a losing run.

AFC Wimbledon are back in League One action on Saturday in search of a second straight home victory to extend their lead over the relegation zone.

The Dons enjoyed a positive start to their second straight campaign in the third tier, earning 12 points from their first eight outings, but they were quickly dragged towards the bottom end of the division, losing four and drawing one of the next five matches.

They scored just three goals in those matches and currently have a league-low tally of 11 goals from 18 games, albeit they were able to make a crucial return to winning ways at home to Blackpool in mid-November, as Alistair Smith's early goal made the only difference.

Johnnie Jackson's men were unable to build on that last time out, though, visiting Leyton Orient and losing 4-1 having trailed by three at the break and pulled one back through Harry Cornick only for Alex Gilbert to put the game out of sight 20 minutes from time.

Now sat 18th, just three points and two places above the bottom four, and with just one league win on the board since mid-September, AFC Wimbledon will again bid to bounce back on Saturday and move further clear of the drop zone and towards mid-table.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head south aiming to arrest a bigger slump which has seen them cut adrift at the bottom of the table.

Daniel Stendel's return to the Barnsley dugout for the 2026-27 season has not gone to plan thus far, as the Yorkshire outfit sit bottom of League One on just nine points from 15 games having won just two and lost 10 of those.

One of those wins and six defeats have come from the Reds' eight away league games thus far, conceding 16 goals in those, while Stendel's men are winless in 11 third-tier outings since early September including three straight defeats heading into the weekend and seven in their last eight.

Following 2-1 losses to Wigan Athletic and South Yorkshire rivals Sheffield Wednesday, they visited Bradford City on Tuesday and suffered a 3-0 beating as Stephen Humphrys scored a brace and Jake Beesley added a late third.

Now rooted to the bottom of the league, four points behind the four teams above them, Barnsley will be desperate to end their long wait for a victory on Saturday and begin climbing towards safety after their dismal start.

AFC Wimbledon form (all competitions):.

Barnsley form (all competitions):.

AFC Wimbledon remain without forward Mathew Stevens due to a long-term injury, while Dujuan Richards and Dan Sweeney are also sidelined.

Attacker Jayden Stockley is back in contention, though, after a suspension last time out, and he will return up front having scored six of the Dons' 11 league goals so far this season.

Cornick will hope to join him, having scored in Stockley's absence at the weekend, with Miles Hippolyte also hoping to continue in an attacking role.

Barnsley are unable to call on attackers Amani Richards, Fabio Jalo and Tobi Adeyemo on Saturday.

Stendel may make changes from the midweek 3-0 loss, with Jubril Okedina in line to return to the defence and Daniel Johnson an option to join Luca Connell in midfield.

That would allow top scorer and captain Cameron McGeehan to return to an advanced midfield role, where he, Reyes Cleary and Vimal Yoganathan may support a lone striker.

AFC Wimbledon possible starting lineup:.

Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa

📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3291 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, from the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when.
  • The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal.
  • “Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, stated of his £55m signing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, from the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, stated of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”.

Industry observers note that in Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

Industry observers note that “I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa stated. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”.

It has been revealed that some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

It has been revealed that the same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

It has been revealed that konsa, 29, has rapidly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

It has been revealed that thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

According to recent reports, the victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also says plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his newly introduced surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

In a recent development, “Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

According to recent reports, “I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”.

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

Recent findings suggest that they kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

According to recent reports, probably sums up Zubimendi’s season so far that he finally gets some meaningful minutes in the Premier League and ends up getting smashed in the face and covered in his own blood. This is after he got injured in a cool-down a few weeks ago. When your luck’s out...

Sources indicate that arsenal have found their groove again, with Madueke twice going close to extending their lead. Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard and Merino are forming a box in midfield and Everton don’t seem to know how to shut them down.

According to recent reports, everton have responded impressively to the Konsa goal and have been the better team since falling behind. Midfielders Garner and Armstrong are growing into the game quite nicely.

Everton have responded well to going behind here. The early goal against them will have ripped up any plans to sit deep and play on the counter.

Set-pieces are back on the menu for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa’s first goal for the club is their first goal from a corner this season, which will come as a relief to set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. “Set piece again, ole ole,” sing the Arsenal fans. Arteta’s side had started the game on the front foot.

Arsenal had not scored from a corner this season... until now. Konsa breaks the deadlock after a melee in the box and his pokes the ball into the net.

It has been revealed that horrible conditions at the Emirates today. The rain has been lashing down. The Emirates drainage system is usually able to cope with this sort of thing. If the wind picks up, that’s likely to be a bigger problem for the two teams.

After a minute’s applause in honour of Ken Friar, the match makes a prompt start at the Emirates.

On bouncing back from defeat...

According to recent reports, “Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”.

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

“They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”.

“Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”.

In a recent development, “A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”.

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

In a recent development, this is presently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

It has been revealed that today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”.

Sources indicate that this is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta remarked: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

Sources indicate that “I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”.

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Sources indicate that moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”.

How Arsenal are evolving their build-up play

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1281 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal have evolved how they attack this season.
  • Recent findings suggest that however, the failure to add true ceiling raising talent in attack this summer- despite heavy interest in Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez- has led to Mikel Arteta needing to coach his way out of a tight spot.
  • Rotations and fluidity Under Mikel Arteta we are accustomed to seeing the left-back enjoy a role based on improvisation and freedom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have evolved how they attack this season. I think there have been quite a few improvements in the way Arsenal seek to create danger that haven’t necessarily shown up on the score board so far. This is an especially sensitive subject this week after draws with Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund- games where Arsenal took deserved one goal leads but failed to build on them.

Recent findings suggest that however, the failure to add true ceiling raising talent in attack this summer- despite heavy interest in Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez- has led to Mikel Arteta needing to coach his way out of a tight spot. The manager has made some alterations to his materials to make Arsenal’s final third play less austere this season. Here are some ways Arteta has evolved the team’s approach play.

Rotations and fluidity Under Mikel Arteta we are accustomed to seeing the left-back enjoy a role based on improvisation and freedom. Last season, we began to see Jurrien Timber take up some very advanced roles from right-back. This stands to reason because full-backs are not typically assigned a marker by the opposition, so it’s easier for full-backs to pop up hither and thither in advanced areas without detection.

Sources indicate that that license has been extended this season. Let’s look at some examples just from the Newcastle game. David Raya releases a long pass here and *squints* who is that playing the role of target man and bringing the long ball down at centre-forward? By God THAT’S EBERECHI EZE’S MUSIC?!

In a recent development, and look who that is sprinting up beside him in the number 10 position but right-back Jurrien Timber. Madueke has a shot and hits the post from this build-up. Look at where Timber is when Madueke takes the shot.

Then we see Odegaard at left-centre-back here (sure, what the hell?) and whose buccaneering forward run is that he is picking out?

Industry observers note that why it’s Riccardo Calafiori. Spotting where Jurrien Timber is when Arsenal have shots on goal has become a favourite pastime of mine. Where’s Jurrien in this shot?

Here he is running down the left-wing to tee Havertz up for a shot.

Sources indicate that this is how the move starts for the Eze goal. Konsa at right-back, Timber at centre-back, Calafiori in central midfield.

When Konsa clips the ball forwards, Madueke has shown for the ball centrally like a number 9 while Havertz has pulled into Madueke’s position. Calafiori continues his run like a horse trotting along without a jockey. You get the message by now, Madueke’s goal in the second half sees Timber make a pass to Havertz in left central midfield.

One of Arsenal’s first shots of the season is created by Tzolis drifting over to the right wing and we had seen Saka manipulated into all sorts of shooting positions prior to his injury. Tzolis was also frustratingly caught offside at St. James’ Park when he had drifted over to the right wing. Hincapie spent a lot of time in central midfield against Borussia Dortmund. Arsenal are a far more fluid outfit this season.

This sense of shapeshifting is reflected in midfield. Rice and Odegaard pretty much always start, the identity of the third midfielder can be any one of Bruno, Lewis Skelly, Zubimendi and Merino, all of whom are high level players with very different qualities. Just the identity of those names gives you face value options.

Declan Rice leads the Premier League for assists this season and all of them have been from open play. That alone tells you something different is happening. Roles in midfield are less defined. There were probably times last season when the Rice and Zubimendi combination became a little too ‘side to side’ and not cutting enough. Spending lots of money on 28-year-old Bruno tells you what Arteta felt his midfield was missing last season- risk and thrust.

Recent findings suggest that bruno expanded on this in the pre-Dortmund press conference, he spoke about the midfield at Arsenal being far less defined positionally, where Rice, Odegaard and AN Other (usually Bruno) will freelance between the 6, 8 and 10 positions. ‘It’s very different. When I was at Newcastle, you play more positional, keep more your position. Here it’s a little bit more free.

‘If you see the game against Newcastle, they were marking us man to man. You see JT [Jurrien Timber] plays a six, an eight and a number nine sometimes, so you have to move a lot. Of course, I was not used to it. So now I understand a little bit more what he wants for the midfield.’ I expanded on midfield a little more in my column from two weeks ago.

Arsenal have not been able to land a genuinely elite attacker in what feels like years now. Fortunately, Arsenal have a manager who might be the best in the trade at this moment in time. As well as moving to a more freestyle approach all over the pitch, there have been signs of improvement in individuals.

It has been revealed that firstly, Noni Madueke seems to be thriving on the opportunities afforded him by Saka’s recent injury. He looks more confident, his actions have greater clarity and Arsenal have treated Madueke as if he is Saka, that is to say, they give him the ball at every opportunity and rely on Noni’s capacity for repetition.

It has been revealed that he is averaging 3.28 shots per 90 in the Premier League this season compared to 1.85 per 90 last season. (He is also averaging fewer crosses per 90 this season which implies an increasing willingness to vary his play and drive at goal as often as he does the by-line). His pass completion rate has jumped by 10% on last season.

Recent findings suggest that the goal against Dortmund saw Madueke cushion a long pass, kill it perfectly and shift it to Gyokeres, who turns and lashes the ball home from 25 yards. That is not a goal description I could have envisaged in September. Gyokeres started the season very badly indeed.

Lewis touched on Gyokeres’ increased creativity this season during the international break. It looks to me as though there has been a focus on him being allowed to offload the ball after one or two touches. You don’t really want the ball getting bogged down with Gyokeres, the more touches he requires the more his technical limitations will show.

Gyokeres gets the ball from a Raya kick here and Madueke is nice and close to him and running in behind.

It means Gyokeres can take one touch and then play in behind. We see something very similar for the chance he creates for Havertz away at Brighton, Havertz is already moving when the ball comes to Gyokeres and it means he can take one touch and hook it in behind.

Then there is his lovely one-touch assist for Declan Rice in Munich where, again, he has a runner very close to him and it allows him to play the ball first time.

Arsenal have also been working on getting Eze in behind and through on goal, look at his position here when Odegaard plays a through ball in Munich.

And look at where he is when he slots Havertz’s lovely slide-rule pass at St. James’ Park.

Industry observers note that getting Eze in on the shoulder of the opposition right-back is another move we are seeing bear fruit sporadically. This fits into a wider theme I touched on a fortnight ago about Arsenal going in behind more often and more rapidly this season.

Juventus and Torino the only Serie A sides without a penalty either way after 11 rounds

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (507 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Juvefc

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino.
  • It has been revealed that juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches.
  • That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

It has been revealed that juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the fresh refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

Sources indicate that the trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, noted it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

In a recent development, close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

The run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool finished the 2025-26 season rather poorly.

They were so bad that Arne Slot was actually relieved of his duties.

Admittedly, this came as a bit of a surprise to most people as fans thought that Fenway Sports Group were going to try and stick with the Dutchman for at least one more season.

Obviously, that didn't end up happening and in the end, Andoni Iraola took over and is presently leading the Reds to a fourth-place finish.

Their performances may have improved but, that doesn't mean that they should settle for fourth, especially since they spent over £150 million on upcoming players in the summer.

Despite this, it's good that things seem to be going well with one of Richard Hughes' last deals potentially saving Liverpool's campaign.

Jeremy Jacquet was a bargain buy from Richard Hughes.

When the £55 million fee for Jeremy Jacquet was first revealed, most people thought that Liverpool massively overspent on him.

The centre-back is only 20 years old and has had no experience of football outside of Ligue 1.

He was also playing for a Rennes team which weren't seen as one of France's best which led many to believe that he was just outperforming his teammates, rather than actually playing well.

However, since coming into Liverpool's starting XI, Jacquet has changed the minds of the doubters and has quickly entered the conversation as one of the Premier League's best-performing defenders.

The Frenchman has played an awful lot of football for Liverpool this term and has had a couple of different partners in the centre of defence.

But, every challenge he has faced has led to his skills improving which is why the Reds' season could have been saved by the youngster.

Liverpool would be a lot worse off without Jeremy Jacquet among their ranks.

As mentioned, Jacquet is now being mentioned as one of the Premier League's best young defenders.

The way that he carries himself on the pitch and the way that he quickly rectifies any mistakes he makes is impressive.

On the ball, he's extremely confident and, if needed, he can ping a pass across the pitch.

Without Jacquet among their ranks, Liverpool would have to start with Joe Gomez or Ronald Araujo in the centre of their defence.

And, while Araujo has played as a centre-back for the Reds this season, if he was used there in each and every game, their right-back situation would be very dicey.

Jeremie Frimpong isn't up to scratch and, with Conor Bradley still side-lined due to injury, someone such as Dominik Szoboszlai or Gomez would have to be played out of position to cover that role.

So, the fact that Jacquet is a Liverpool player is a massive help to them and is likely one of the main reasons why they're only seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

Erling Haaland cut a despondent figure as he admitted to 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli continued their underwhelming form.

'The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy.

Haaland admitted in another interview with Bein Sports that the run of form 'hurts', with the star having offered a resigned laugh when asked whether the draw against Napoli should be considered a 'good point'.

'We have to do better and find some ways to control the game more and perform in a better way.

Industry observers note that man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Man City face Arsenal in a crucial match on Sunday as they look to make inroads in the Gunners six point lead at the top of the Premier League.

Haaland had pushed back against suggestions the case had affected their form during the international break, while stressing he was committed long-term to the club.

According to recent reports, 'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland stated.

It has been revealed that 'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle….

'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'.

He continued: 'It's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

In a recent development, 'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

The Man City star, who signed a nine-and-a-half-year contract in late 2024, told Norwegian television earlier this month that his focus was on helping the team to turn their form around.

The draw against Napoli leaves Man City lying sixth in the Champions League table - which would be enough to see Maresca's side to qualify for the last-16.

Man City face a crucial clash on the weekend when they face reigning champions Arsenal in the Premier League, as they look to halve the six-point gap to the leaders at the top of the table.

Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 57 min read (11474 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~57 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide1,2,3,4, yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood.
  • Shifts in the distribution of tree species in response to climate change1,2 and disturbances3,4 can substantially affect forest structure, biodiversity and ecosystem services5,6,7,8.
  • In a recent development, forests in the western USA span a broad elevational range, from near sea level to approximately 3,700 m, near the upper treeline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide1,2,3,4, yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999–2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species’ elevational ranges: upper portions of species’ ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres revealed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

Shifts in the distribution of tree species in response to climate change1,2 and disturbances3,4 can substantially affect forest structure, biodiversity and ecosystem services5,6,7,8. Such redistribution can be characterized by shifts in tree abundance centres, which reveals how populations reorganize within their ranges2,9,10. Given that cooler conditions occur at higher latitudes and elevations, poleward and upslope shifts in species distribution are expected with climate change1,9,10,11,12. However, downslope shifts of tree species in montane ecosystems have also been reported, probably reflecting the influence of non-temperature factors that alter tree abundance and distribution in contrasting ways13,14,15,16. Natural disturbances, such as wildfires, diseases and insect outbreaks, along with subsequent regeneration, can alter stem abundance and basal area (the cross-sectional surface area of tree trunks measured at breast height—1.37 m above the ground) across regions4, influencing latitudinal or longitudinal shifts3. Yet, the roles of disturbances in shaping species’ elevational redistribution remains underexplored8.

In a recent development, forests in the western USA span a broad elevational range, from near sea level to approximately 3,700 m, near the upper treeline. Over recent decades, these forests have experienced pronounced warming and frequent droughts17,18, which have increased wildfire activity19,20 and insect outbreaks21,22, and altered forest disease patterns22,23. As these disturbances can alter tree demographic dynamics4, elevational variation in disturbance activity may drive the elevational redistribution of tree abundance. Moreover, warming may shift disturbance patterns23,24,25, further influencing tree abundance redistribution. Although previous studies have reported elevational shifts across regions, most have been restricted geographically with inconsistent patterns9,14,26,27,28. A comprehensive and cross-regional assessment using a consistent methodology remains lacking, which limits our understanding of elevational shift patterns and their underlying mechanisms in the context of environmental change.

It has been revealed that to fill this gap, we quantified elevational shifts in tree abundance centres of common tree species across individual ecosections (ecoregion sections) in the western USA using remeasured plots conducted by the US Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) programme29. As the western USA spans a vast climatic and ecological gradient and encompasses diverse forest types, estimating elevational shifts across the entire region would mask regional-scale differences and could be confounded by species’ geographical redistribution among regions14,30,31,32. We therefore conducted our analyses separately within individual ecosections for each species. By selecting tree species that occurred in more than 100 remeasured FIA plots without evidence of silvicultural treatment within individual montane ecosections (Fig. 1a), we identified 45 species (Extended Data Table 1) across 33 ecosections, yielding 212 species–ecosection combinations. Collectively, they accounted for 68% of total stems and 69% of total basal area across montane forests in the western USA.

a, Map of montane ecoregion provinces and sections. Letters indicate the section code in each ecoregion province. Only ecosections with species represented by more than 100 remeasured plots are shaded. These ecosections occur within the following montane provinces: M242 (Cascade Mixed Forest), M261 (Sierran Steppe), M313 (Arizona–Upcoming Mexico Mountains Steppe), M331 (Southern Rocky Mountain Steppe), M332 (Middle Rocky Mountain Steppe), M333 (Northern Rocky Mountain Forest) and M341 (Nevada–Utah Mountain Steppe). b, Distributions of elevational shifts in basal area (left) and stem abundance (right) of 212 species–ecosections. The proportions of total stems or basal area with significant downslope (brown) and upslope (green) shifts are annotated. c, Mean shift rates in individual ecosections, weighted by basal area (left) and stem abundance (right) across species. Light blue shading is to distinguish ecoregion provinces. d, Mean shift rates for each species, weighted by basal area (left) and stem abundance (right) across ecosections. Light blue shading is to distinguish different genera. Symbol size in c and d denotes relative tree abundance, calculated as the proportion of basal area or stem abundance relative to the total. In b–d, brown and green denote significant (P < 0.05) downslope and upslope shifts, respectively, and grey indicates shifts that are not significant (NS). In d, species are shown in phylogenetic order. Statistical significance of elevational shifts was assessed using two-sided paired bootstrap tests with 10,000 resamples. Scale bar, 500 km.

In this study, we aimed to address three objectives: (1) to characterize patterns of elevational shifts in tree abundance centres across species–ecosections in the western USA under climate change and natural disturbances; (2) to examine how climate and disturbance jointly influence tree abundance changes and (3) to evaluate how elevational asymmetries in climate and disturbance activity influence the elevational redistribution of tree abundance. We quantified elevational shifts for individual species–ecosections using two measures of tree abundance: basal area and stem abundance. For each measure, the shift was calculated as the difference in species’ elevational centres between two inventory periods (T1, 1999–2013 and T2, 2012–2025), yielding the basal area shift and stem shift. Changes in stem abundance and basal area both reflect demographic processes but differ in their sensitivity to tree size classes. Stem abundance may be influenced more strongly by sapling dynamics (mortality and ingrowth), as saplings are typically more numerous than adult trees. Here, ingrowth refers to the entry of stems into a specified size class by crossing a diameter threshold as defined by the FIA: sapling ingrowth occurs when stems enter the 2.54–12.7 cm diameter at breast height (DBH) class, and adult ingrowth occurs when stems grow beyond 12.7 cm DBH. FIA ingrowth therefore represents the combined outcome of earlier recruitment, survival and growth sufficient for an individual to cross an inventory threshold. Basal area gives greater weight to larger trees and is influenced more strongly by the growth and mortality of adult trees. Thus, the two measures provide complementary information on population change. Because shifts in abundance centre ultimately arise from asymmetric tree abundance changes along species’ elevational gradients, understanding the drivers of plot-level tree abundance change is essential for interpreting the mechanisms underlying these shifts. We then assessed the effects of changes in mean annual temperature (MAT) and drought frequency, together with disturbance factors including fire, insect outbreaks and disease, on plot-level tree abundance changes. Finally, we investigated the elevational asymmetries in these environmental factors, defined as differences between elevational segments above (upper) and below (lower) the elevational centre at T1, and evaluated their associations with ecosection-level elevational shifts using generalized linear mixed models.

Elevational redistribution of basal area and stem abundance varied substantially among species–ecosections, with many showing little change in elevational centres whereas others exhibited significant upslope or downslope shifts (Extended Data Fig. 1). For basal area, shifts were more often downslope than upslope: 42 of 212 species–ecosections shifted significantly (P < 0.05) downslope and 28 shifted upslope, representing 30% and 11% of total basal area across all focal species–ecosections, respectively. When aggregating all species within individual ecosections, 12 of the total 33 ecosections shifted downslope, whereas four ecosections shifted upslope (Fig. 1c). Except for the Nevada–Utah Mountain Steppe (M341), downslope shifts were more common than upslope shifts across ecoregion provinces (Fig. 1c). When aggregating across ecosections by species, 16 species (61.5% total basal area) experienced a significant downslope shift and 11 (11.3% total basal area) shifted upslope. Among the eight most dominant species, six shifted downslope (P < 0.05), including Pseudotsuga menziesii (Douglas fir), Pinus ponderosa (ponderosa pine), Pinus contorta (lodgepole pine), Tsuga heterophylla (western hemlock), Picea engelmannii (Engelmann spruce) and Abies concolor (white fir), whereas none shifted upslope (Fig. 1d).

When measured by stem abundance, shift in elevational centre was more divergent. Specifically, 23 species–ecosections moved downslope and 22 upslope (Extended Data Fig. 1), representing 7.4% and 10.7% of total stem abundance across all focal species–ecosections, respectively (Fig. 1b). Spatially, five ecosections exhibited significant overall downslope shifts, whereas six ecosections highlighted significant upslope shifts (Fig. 1c). At the species level, only three species shifted downslope and six shifted upslope (Fig. 1d), reflecting divergent elevational responses among ecosections within individual species (Extended Data Fig. 1).

Industry observers note that to understand demographic changes underlying the observed elevational shifts, we examined range-edge dynamics by comparing relative tree abundance change between the upper and lower range segments for species–ecosections with significant shifts (Extended Data Fig. 2). Upper and lower range segments were defined as portions of a species’ range above and below the elevational centre weighted by basal area or stem abundance from the initial inventory (T1). For basal area, 61% of upslope shifts and 69% of downslope shifts were associated with consistent changes of basal area in upper and lower segments (either both declining or both increasing, but at differing rates above versus below the elevational centre). For stem abundance, 64% of upslope shifts were associated with declines at lower and increases at upper-range segments, whereas 57% of downslope shifts showed the opposite pattern. This indicates that stem shifts are associated with asymmetric demographic responses between cooler (upper) and warmer (lower) elevational segments, with increase in abundance at one end coupled with decline at the other.

Industry observers note that we further analysed the tree abundance change at upper and lower ranges for saplings and adult trees, separately. The asymmetric responses of saplings between range segments aligned with stem-based shifts, whereas those of adults aligned with basal area shifts, indicating that stem shifts were driven primarily by changes in sapling abundance and basal area shifts were driven primarily by changes in adult basal area (Extended Data Fig. 2b). Results were similar when using plots in the uppermost and lowermost 25% of elevations (Supplementary Fig. 1).

Industry observers note that as uneven changes in tree abundance along elevational gradients drive shifts in abundance centre, we examined how plot-level changes in tree abundance were associated with climate change and disturbance history. From the recent past (1983–2002, as a baseline) to the study period (2003–2022), MAT in the study region increased by an average of 0.7 °C (Extended Data Fig. 3). Drought frequency, determined based on the 12-month Standardized Precipitation–Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) in July (SPEI12July), generally increased, with the largest increases in southern provinces. Based on FIA records, recent disturbances recorded at T2 (less than or equal to 10 years before revisit) and legacy disturbances recorded at T1 (10–15 years before revisit) indicated similar spatial patterns, but legacy disturbances affected smaller forest areas overall (Extended Data Fig. 4).

A generalized linear mixed model fitted across all species–ecosections revealed that climate, disturbance and their interactions were key drivers of stem abundance change (Fig. 2). Increases in temperature and drought frequency exerted modest but opposing influences on stem abundance: warming corresponded to gains, whereas greater drought frequency corresponded to losses. Baseline drought frequency partially mitigated the negative effects of increasing drought frequency on stem abundance, suggesting that forests historically exposed to more frequent droughts were more resistant to additional water stress.

a–f, Generalized linear mixed model coefficients are presented as percentage changes in stem abundance between inventories associated with a 1 s.d. increase in each predictor for all trees (a), saplings (c) and adults (e) (n = 74,448 samples for each analysis). Points, model coefficient estimates; error bars, 95% confidence intervals (CIs). All predictors except plant clade were standardized to zero mean and unit standard deviation before modelling; plant clade was included as a categorical predictor using sum-to-zero contrasts (angiosperm = 1, gymnosperm = −1). Positive coefficients (blue) indicate increases in stem abundance, whereas negative coefficients (red) indicate declines. Light grey shading is to distinguish three predictor categories (from top to bottom: climate, natural disturbances and others, which includes interactions between disturbances and climate variables or plant attributes). Solid lines, model-predicted mean percentage changes in stem abundance; shaded bands, 95% CIs. In the models, ΔMAT and ΔDrought represent changes in MAT and drought frequency, respectively, from the baseline (1983–2002) to the study (2003–2022) period; drought frequency is the number of years per decade with SPEI12July < −1.0. Fire, disease and insect variables indicate the proportion of forest area affected by each disturbance before T1 (legacy) or between T1 and T2 (recent). Statistical significance in a, c and e was assessed using two-sided Wald z-tests without adjustment for multiple comparisons. Significance levels are indicated as ***P < 0.001, **P < 0.01, *P < 0.05 and #P < 0.1. Exact P values are provided in the Source Data. Effects of the full model are provided in Extended Data Fig. 5.

Disturbances exerted strong effects on changes in stem abundance, and these effects differed between recent and legacy disturbances (Fig. 2). Recent fires were associated with the largest reductions in stem abundance, whereas legacy fires increased stem abundance, probably reflecting forest regeneration from earlier fires. Disease had generally weak effects, but legacy disease was associated with stronger negative effects than recent disease, suggesting more persistent impacts of earlier disease events. Conversely, recent insect outbreaks were associated with larger reductions in stem abundance than legacy outbreaks, consistent with partial recovery following earlier outbreaks. Moreover, where previous disease and insect outbreaks had occurred, recent fires were associated with greater declines in stem abundance (Extended Data Fig. 5), suggesting interactive and compounding disturbance impacts.

Recent findings suggest that fire effects also interacted with other factors including baseline drought, species’ fire tolerance and plant clade (angiosperm or gymnosperm) (Fig. 2). Specifically, fires in historically dry areas were associated with smaller reductions in stem abundance, probably because lower vegetation productivity and fuel availability in dry forests can limit fire severity and associated mortality33. Recent fire effects also depended on species’ functional traits, with fire-tolerant species experiencing smaller declines following recent fires. Legacy fire was associated positively with stem abundance in both plant clades, with substantially stronger responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms (Fig. 2a,b). Despite some variation, models in individual provinces were largely consistent with the overall effects (Extended Data Fig. 6).

Sources indicate that to evaluate potential life-stage differences in responses to environmental change, we also modelled stem abundance change separately for saplings and adult trees (Fig. 2 and Extended Data Fig. 5). Warming primarily promoted sapling abundance but had little influence on adult abundance. Although recent fires consistently caused declines in both saplings and adults, legacy fires showed a positive effect on sapling abundance but a negative effect on adults. This indicates regeneration events after legacy fires, but many recruits are still below the 12.7 cm DBH threshold at plot remeasurement (10–15 years after fire). Disease decreased adult stem abundance; recent disease had little effect on saplings and legacy disease was associated with reduced sapling abundance. Legacy fire effects on stem abundance differed between saplings and adults, and between angiosperms and gymnosperms. Legacy fire was associated with increased stem abundance in saplings, with substantially stronger responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. By contrast, legacy fire slightly reduced adult stem abundance, with no significant difference observed between angiosperms and gymnosperms (Fig. 2d,f).

In a recent development, models of basal area dynamics showed patterns similar to adult stem abundance (Extended Data Figs. 7 and 8), reflecting a strong contribution of large trees to basal area. While MAT change had a marginally positive effect on basal area change (P = 0.056), drought frequency change and most disturbance factors showed negative effects, except for the non-significant effect of recent disease and positive effect of legacy fire. The positive effect of legacy fire was driven primarily by angiosperms, whereas gymnosperms showed relatively weak responses (Extended Data Fig. 7b,d).

In a recent development, to further understand the mechanisms underlying elevational shifts in tree abundance centres, we investigated how climate change and disturbance were distributed across species’ elevational gradients. We hypothesized that, rather than the average changes in environmental drivers across elevations, uneven exposure to the environmental changes between upper and lower range segments drives the observed elevational shifts in tree abundance centres. To test this hypothesis, we quantified differences in changes in climate (MAT and drought frequency) and disturbance extent between the two elevational segments (above and below the elevational centre at T1) for individual species–ecosections.

Overall, trees in upper-range segments experienced greater climate change and more extensive disturbance than in lower segments (Fig. 3). The upper–lower difference in the change in MAT (ΔMAT) was significantly positive for all the ecoregion provinces, indicating stronger warming at higher elevations (Fig. 3a). For drought frequency, lower range segments generally had higher values than upper segments during the baseline period (1983–2002), but this pattern partially reversed during the study period (2003–2022), with more ecoregion provinces showing higher drought frequency in upper segments (Supplementary Fig. 2). Consistent with this shift, temporal increases in drought frequency (ΔDrought) were greater in upper than lower species ranges in four ecoregion provinces, including Cascade Mixed Forest (M242), Sierran Steppe (M261), Arizona–Newly introduced Mexico Mountains Steppe (M313) and Northern Rocky Mountain Forest (M333) (Fig. 3b).

In each boxplot, the centre line indicates the median, the lower and upper bounds of the box indicate the 25th and 75th percentiles, respectively, and the whiskers extend to the smallest and largest values within 1.5× the interquartile range from the lower and upper hinges; values beyond the whiskers are shown individually in grey. Upper and lower range segments are defined as the elevational range above and below the elevational centre at T1. It has been revealed that patterns of disturbance asymmetry varied by type and period (Fig. 3c–h). Notably, recent fire and disease exhibited significantly (P < 0.05) positive upper–lower differences in more provinces than their legacy counterparts. Specifically, recent fires affected larger proportions of forest area in the upper range in three of the seven ecoregion provinces, whereas the lower range was more affected in only one province (Fig. 3f). By contrast, there was no clear evidence showing the elevational asymmetry in legacy fire. Recent disease affected larger upper-range proportions in three provinces (Fig. 3g), compared with two provinces for legacy disease (Fig. 3d). Both legacy and recent insect outbreaks were more prevalent in upper-range segments in three provinces.

It has been revealed that we then modelled elevational shift rate in basal area and stem abundance, with species–ecosections as observational units and upper–lower asymmetries in climate change and disturbance as predictors (Fig. 4 and Extended Data Fig. 9). For basal area shifts, upper–lower difference in recent fire extent and insect outbreak extent highlighted significantly negative effects (P < 0.01), indicating that greater disturbance extents at one end of elevational range tended to displace population centres towards the opposite end. Elevational asymmetry in legacy fire showed a marginally significant positive effect on basal area shift on average (P = 0.053). The effect differed significantly between angiosperms and gymnosperms, with stronger upslope redistribution observed in angiosperms (Fig. 4a,b). Plant clade also showed a strong main effect, with angiosperms exhibiting more pronounced upslope shifts than gymnosperms under average covariate conditions across species–ecosections.
