According to recent reports, for stem shifts, upper–lower difference in ΔDrought, recent fire extent and legacy insect extent showed negative effects. Asymmetric warming (ΔMAT) showed a positive but non-significant association with elevational shift (P = 0.19), implying that warming may promote upslope movement weakly but is probably overshadowed by disturbance and increasing drought frequency. Interaction effects further revealed that species with higher fire tolerance were less sensitive to elevational asymmetry of recent fire extent, consistent with trait-mediated resilience to disturbance. Elevational asymmetry in legacy fire extent also showed a positive effect, suggesting that a greater legacy fire extent at one end of the elevational range was associated with a shift of the elevational centre towards the same end, potentially reflecting post-fire regeneration within previously burned areas. This positive effect was marginally stronger in angiosperms than in gymnosperms (Fig. 4c,d). Similar to basal area shifts, the main effect of plant clade indicated that angiosperms generally exhibited more pronounced upslope shifts than gymnosperms.

Across 212 species–ecosection combinations spanning broad climatic and biogeographical gradients in the western USA, many tree abundance centres remained relatively stable despite ongoing climate change and natural disturbance. This relative stability probably reflected opposing demographic processes, with ingrowth and growth promoted by warming and post-disturbance recovery counterbalanced by mortality associated with drought and disturbance. Where redistribution occurred, stem shifts were divergent, whereas basal area shifts were more commonly downslope (Fig. 1). Stem abundance is influenced more strongly by sapling ingrowth, whereas basal area is linked more closely to larger tree dynamics. The discrepancy between stem and basal area shifts suggests a general upslope redistribution of smaller trees relative to larger trees, consistent with previous findings that seedlings tend to occupy higher elevations than adults28. Elevational shifts in tree abundance centre arise from asymmetric changes in abundance along species’ elevational gradients (Extended Data Fig. 2) and therefore reflect demographic redistribution within species ranges in response to environment change.

According to recent reports, our findings demonstrate that both climate change and natural disturbances, along with their interactions, are key drivers of tree abundance dynamics across the forests of the western USA. The strong negative effects of increasing drought frequency align with extensive evidence of drought-induced mortality and reduced growth under water stress34,35,36. In historically drought-prone areas, drought effects on stem abundance were weaker, consistent with evidence that previous or recurrent drought may enhance resistance to subsequent water stress through stress-memory mechanisms37. This pattern was more evident for sapling abundance than for adult stem abundance, suggesting that drought history may alter the balance between sapling mortality and sapling ingrowth more strongly. By contrast, warming exhibited positive effects on stem abundance, driven largely by enhanced sapling ingrowth or reduced sapling mortality (Fig. 2 and Extended Data Fig. 5). This pattern suggests that temperature increases can promote regeneration where moisture remains sufficient38, which often occurs in cooler or higher-elevation sites.

It has been revealed that although fires, disease and insect outbreaks all reduce tree abundance, their effects unfold differently over time. Biotic disturbances such as disease and insect outbreaks caused prolonged declines, as pathogens and pests can persist for years and continue to kill trees39. By contrast, fires triggered abrupt losses in tree abundance followed by gradual increases during post-fire recovery and regeneration40. Our comparison of recent and legacy disturbances is limited to events recorded by the FIA annual inventory, which captures only a relatively recent disturbance history before plot remeasurement. Because post-disturbance recovery can unfold over longer time scales, earlier events not recorded in the FIA disturbance history may also have contributed to tree abundance redistribution but could not be evaluated directly in our analysis.

According to recent reports, post-fire regeneration has an crucial role in changing stem abundance and elevational distributions, but its effects differed markedly between angiosperms and gymnosperms (Fig. 2). The relatively weak responses of gymnosperms to legacy fires are consistent with recent studies reporting widespread post-fire regeneration failure of gymnosperms in warm, dry and often low-elevation forests in the western USA41,42. When regeneration thresholds are crossed, fire can act as a tipping point: instead of returning to closed-canopy forest, sites may transition to shrubland, grassland or sparse woodland. By contrast, angiosperms showed relatively stronger positive responses to legacy fire, which aligns with the greater capacity for vegetative resprouting of many angiosperms following fires43. Such contrasting post-fire responses suggest that fires may increasingly promote divergent elevational redistribution between angiosperms and gymnosperms.

Although climate change and disturbance pressures drive tree abundance changes, their elevational asymmetry (differences between upper and lower range segments) emerged as an important predictor of the direction and magnitude of species’ elevational shifts (Fig. 4). Processes that reduce tree abundance including increasing drought frequency and recent disturbances can shift population centres away from the affected end of a species’ elevational range, whereas processes that enhance tree abundance such as warming and post-disturbance recovery at one end pull population centres towards the affected end. Under natural disturbance, stronger pressures in upper-range segments across the western USA (Fig. 3) were associated with more frequent downslope shifts in basal area. When plots affected by silvicultural treatments were included, however, basal area shifts were distributed more evenly between upslope and downslope directions (Supplementary Fig. 5), possibly reflecting the greater prevalence of timber harvest at lower elevations8. These results suggest that the elevational distributions can be modified by other elevationally asymmetric influences, including human activities. By explicitly quantifying these asymmetric environmental pressures rather than relying on area-averaged climate trends and disturbance, our approach captures the spatial heterogeneity that shapes demographic processes directly at species’ range segments. Although conceptually intuitive, such asymmetry has rarely been incorporated explicitly into broad-scale assessments of species redistribution. Our findings highlight the need to consider not only regional trends in climate and disturbance, but also how these pressures are distributed across elevation gradients.

Industry observers note that overall, natural disturbances and drought had stronger effects than warming in our models, probably reflecting differences in the time scales of demographic processes, including mortality, ingrowth and growth. Although natural disturbances and drought can reduce tree abundance rapidly through mortality, increases in stem abundance through ingrowth and in basal area through growth accumulate over time. Given the relatively short remeasurement interval (approximately 10 years) in this study, sapling ingrowth may be more evident than adult ingrowth, which may partly explain why adult stem abundance was less sensitive to warming and legacy disturbance than sapling abundance42. These differences in temporal sensitivity may also contribute to the different patterns of stem and basal area shifts. Basal area shifts, which are dominated by larger trees, were more commonly downslope and associated with greater disturbance activity in upper-range segments (Fig. 3). By contrast, stem shifts were more divergent, probably because sapling ingrowth can offset mortality losses more rapidly in smaller trees. Similar demographic differences may also underlie the contrasting redistribution patterns between plant clades. Angiosperms, which generally exhibit stronger recruitment and post-disturbance recovery43, showed greater upslope redistribution than gymnosperms (Fig. 4b,d). This underscores the importance of long-term monitoring, as repeated measurements over longer intervals are essential for capturing the full demographic imprint of sustained warming and disturbance on species redistribution.

In a recent development, climate change may have exerted indirect effects on forest redistribution by altering disturbance regimes and their elevational distributions19,44,45. Although lower elevations in forests in the western USA were generally drier than higher elevations during the baseline period (1983–2002), drought frequency has increased disproportionately in upper-range segments in recent decades (Fig. 3 and Supplementary Fig. 2). This increase in drought frequency, together with stronger warming in species’ upper-range segments, may help explain the greater fire activity observed there23,24,46. Consistent with our findings, wildfires in the western USA have advanced upslope at an average rate of 7.6 m per year between 1984 and 2017 (ref. 24). Moreover, elevated winter temperatures have enabled mountain pine beetle (Dendroctonus ponderosae) to survive at higher elevations than previously possible, exposing previously less affected high-elevation forests to greater pest pressure47.

Our study underscores the substantial influence of disturbances, particularly wildfires and insect outbreaks, on tree abundance and elevational redistribution. Recent disturbances were often associated with reduced tree abundance, driving abundance centres shifting downslope. Meanwhile, climate warming and post-fire recovery tended to increase tree abundance, and post-fire recovery was associated with upslope shifts in tree abundance centres. Therefore, the combined pressures from climate change and disturbances place forest ecosystems in the western USA ‘between a rock and a hard place’. Given projected future climate change and increasing disturbance activities globally45, our findings highlight the need for continued monitoring and adaptive forest management strategies to mitigate these impacts and promote ecosystem sustainability and resilience.

Industry observers note that the annual inventory of the FIA programme uses a nationally consistent plot design (around 1 plot per 2,428 hectares (ha)) and provides remeasurements with consistent data collection procedures nationwide, enabling robust estimation of changes in forest structure and species distribution. Each FIA plot consists of four 168 m2 subplots on which adult trees (DBH ≥ 12.7 cm) are measured. Within each subplot, a 13.5 m2 microplot is nested to sample saplings (2.54 cm ≤ DBH < 12.7 cm)29. For some plots, additional macroplots are established to measure very large trees. To account for differences in sampling area among microplots, subplots and macroplots, we used the trees-per-acre expansion factors provided by FIA, which standardize tree abundance estimates to a common per-area basis. We obtained forest attributes from the initial inventory period (T1, 1999–2013) and the subsequent remeasurement period (T2, 2012–2025). Because forest management can influence regional patterns of tree density, we excluded plots that showed evidence of recent silvicultural activity, including harvesting, artificial regeneration or site preparation. A total of 44,368 forest plots located within montane ecoregions were selected across 11 western US states (Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana, Wyoming, California, Utah, Nevada, Colorado, Arizona and New Mexico). The average interval between measurements was approximately 10 years.

According to recent reports, elevational shifts were quantified within individual species–ecosection combinations, rather than across the entire western US, to avoid conflating elevational shifts with latitudinal shifts. Ecoregion boundaries followed the US Forest Service 2007 ecoregion map48. We selected 45 tree species that occurred in more than 100 remeasured FIA plots without evidence of silvicultural treatment within individual montane ecosections, yielding 212 species–ecosection combinations across 33 ecosections. For each species–ecosection, elevational shifts were quantified as the difference in the stem abundance-weighted or basal area-weighted elevational centres of all trees (DBH ≥ 2.54 cm) between the two inventory periods. The shift rate (metres per decade) was calculated by dividing the elevational shift distance by the mean remeasurement interval of plots where the target species was present. To examine spatial and taxonomic patterns, we further aggregated species–ecosection elevational shifts to the ecosection and species levels. For stem shifts, the mean shift for each aggregation was calculated using stem abundance as a weighting factor, whereas basal area was used as the weight for basal area shifts.

Industry observers note that because ecosection boundaries can intersect species’ elevational ranges, particularly at lower elevations, they may influence the observed elevational shifts by truncating portions of species distributions. To evaluate the potential impact of this boundary effect, we conducted a sensitivity analysis by extending montane ecosections into adjacent non-montane regions using spatial buffers. We applied buffer widths of 50 km and 100 km, which correspond roughly to the average width of counties in the western USA and are appropriate given the spatial uncertainty associated with FIA plot coordinate swapping within counties. Elevational shifts were recalculated under each buffering scenario and compared with the original estimates based on unbuffered ecosections. The overall distribution of elevational shifts remained highly consistent among the 0 km, 50 km and 100 km buffering scenarios (Supplementary Fig. 6). Therefore, we retained the original Bailey’s ecosections as the primary study units because buffering produced little change in the overall patterns.

In a recent development, this study aimed to examine how natural processes, including climate change and natural disturbances, influence tree elevational redistribution in montane forests in the western USA. Because silvicultural treatments often depend on local management objectives, ownership and socioeconomic conditions, we excluded plots that showed evidence of recent silvicultural activity from the main analysis. As a sensitivity analysis, we repeated the elevational shift calculations with these plots included. This analysis produced more upslope shifts in basal area centres than the treatment-excluded analysis, resulting in a more balanced number of upslope and downslope shifts (Supplementary Fig. 5), possibly reflecting low-elevation timber harvest8. We therefore focused on the treatment-excluded analysis to minimize the influence of silvicultural treatments and better evaluate tree redistribution associated primarily with climate change and natural disturbances.

Sources indicate that to test whether the observed shifts in elevational centre were statistically significant, we used a non-parametric bootstrap resampling approach3,49,50. For each species–ecosection combination, FIA plots were treated as the resampling unit, and paired T1 and T2 observations were resampled together with replacement using the original sample size (Supplementary Table 1). In each iteration, elevational centres for both inventory periods and the resulting elevational shift were recalculated. This procedure was repeated 10,000 times to generate a bootstrap distribution of elevational shift estimates. From the distribution, we derived percentile-based 95% CIs and corresponding empirical two-tailed P values. A shift was considered significant when the 95% CI did not include zero. The two-tailed P value was calculated as twice the smaller proportion of bootstrap estimates greater or less than 0, representing the probability of observing a shift as extreme as the empirical value under the null hypothesis of no change.

Recent findings suggest that in the FIA, plots are divided into conditions representing distinct landscape units based on attributes identified by field crews, such as ownership, land type (for example, forest, water) and evidence of disturbance. The proportional area of each condition within a plot is recorded. The FIA database records disturbance events on mapped forest conditions, such as fire, insect outbreak and disease, that occurred since the last measurement in a remeasurement or within the last 5 years for new plots. Only disturbance events affecting at least 1 acre (0.4 ha) in size (including both the plot and adjacent affected areas) and causing mortality or damage to at least 25% of trees were recorded51. Based on the recorded condition proportions, we calculated the total forest area and that disturbed by any of the three principal disturbance agents including fire, insect outbreak and disease in each plot at both the initial inventory (T1; legacy) and remeasured inventory (T2; recent). On average, legacy and recent fires occurred 13.1 and 4.1 years before the T2 remeasurement, respectively. Note that one plot could experience more than one type of disturbance agent, and the area was attributed to each agent based on its specific disturbance, resulting in possible overlap among disturbance agents. For each species–ecosection, we summed forest area and disturbed area from plots using FIA-defined expansion factors with the target species present and calculated the disturbance extent as the proportion of disturbed forest area to the total forest area at both inventories.

For climate variables, we used 800-m resolution monthly temperature data from the PRISM Climate Group Long-Term dataset52 (https://data.prism.oregonstate.edu/time_series/us/lt/800m/) and 4-km SPEI12July from the WestWide Drought Tracker53 (https://wrcc.app/climate/wwdt/archives). The PRISM long-term dataset was used because it is based only on long-term stations of record and is therefore considered more temporally stable than the PRISM All-Network dataset54. SPEI is a drought index calculated as difference between precipitation and potential evapotranspiration over a specified time period55. SPEI12July was used because it is correlated strongly with tree mortality and growth56,57,58,59,60. Drought events were determined as years with SPEI12July < −1.0 (refs. 57,58,61,62,63,64). MAT and drought frequency (number of drought years per decade) were calculated in the recent past (1983–2002) for a baseline and the study period (2003–2022). Climate change was calculated as the difference between these two periods, accounting for potential lags between climatic trends and vegetation responses1,65. For each species–ecosection, climate variables were extracted from all plots where the species occurred and averaged to obtain ecosection-level estimates.

True FIA plot coordinates are not released publicly to ensure ecological integrity and protect landowner privacy. Instead, the publicly available FIA data apply a ‘fuzzing and swapping’ protocol. On public lands, plot locations are displaced randomly, typically by less than 0.8 km and rarely up to 1.6 km. For private lands, up to 20% of plots are swapped with another plot of similar attributes within the same county. Although these procedures introduce spatial uncertainty, their influence on our analyses is expected to be negligible for several reasons. First, plot elevation in the FIA data is generally accurate, and our analysis of elevational shifts relies on repeated measurements of the same plots, for which elevation remains constant across inventories. Second, around 76% of the plots used in this study occur on public lands with location offsets (<0.8 km). Although these offsets may introduce climate uncertainty because elevation and vegetation types can vary substantially within a single 0.8- or 4-km pixel, such mismatches are expected to be largely random across the large number of FIA plots (44,368) and therefore have limited influence on the overall conclusions of this study. Finally, for private plots, the swapping process pairs plots with similar forest type, stand size, latitude and longitude, ensuring that local climatic and ecological conditions remain comparable.

We computed elevational asymmetry for relative tree abundance change (Extended Data Fig. 2), climate change and disturbance extent (Fig. 3) by calculating their difference between upper and lower range segments. Relative tree abundance change between T1 and T2 was quantified for stem abundance and basal area as a symmetric percent change, which places increase and decreases on a common scale (the average of T1 and T2) and avoids the asymmetry of conventional percent change66. Upper and lower range segments are defined as the elevational range above and below the elevational centre weighted by stem abundance or basal area from the initial inventory (T1). We also conducted analysis using plots within the uppermost and lowermost 25% of elevations and found similar patterns (Supplementary Figs. 1, 3 and 4).

Species attributes of fire tolerance, drought tolerance and plant clade (angiosperm or gymnosperm) were obtained from the US Department of Agriculture PLANTS Database (https://plants.sc.egov.usda.gov/). In PLANTS, fire tolerance qualitatively describes a species’ ability to survive or recover from fire and is classified into four levels: None, Low, Medium and High. Similarly, drought tolerance, describing a species’ ability to survive or maintain function under low soil moisture, is categorized into three levels: Low, Medium and High. For the four species lacking trait entries in PLANTS (Juniperus deppeana, Quercus arizonica, Quercus wislizeni and Quercus grisea), tolerance classes were assigned on the basis of expert knowledge. Detailed information on species attributes is provided in Extended Data Table 1.

Recent findings suggest that we used a non-parametric Wilcoxon signed-rank test to evaluate whether the upper–lower differences in climate change and disturbance extent were significantly different from zero (Fig. 2). We modelled the plot-level change in stem abundance and basal area between inventories using the log response ratio (LRR):.

In a recent development, where \({M}_{T1}\) and \({M}_{T2}\) denote the values of stem abundance or basal area measured at T1 and T2, respectively, and c is a small pseudocount (set to 0.5 in this study) to avoid division by zero. Models were fitted in R using the glmmTMB67 package (v.1.1.10) with a Gaussian error distribution and identity link. Fixed effects included baseline climate and climate changes for MAT and drought frequency derived from SPEI12July, disturbance extents by fire, disease and insects during T1 (legacy) and T2 (recent), and species attributes including fire tolerance, drought tolerance and plant clade (angiosperm or gymnosperm). We also included interactions between baseline climate and climate changes, between baseline drought frequency and recent disturbance extent, and between disturbance and species attributes. Fire and drought tolerance classes were converted to continuous variables to facilitate model fitting. Plant clade was included as a categorical predictor using sum-to-zero contrasts (angiosperm = 1, gymnosperm = −1). All predictors except plant clade are standardized to zero mean and unit standard deviation before modelling. Species and ecosection were included as random effects. Because the models included several interaction terms (for example, climate change versus baseline climate), we evaluated collinearity among predictors using variance inflation factor. All predictors variance inflation factors less than 5, indicating acceptable collinearity, and no variables were excluded from the final models. For interpretability, model coefficients and their 95% CIs were later back-transformed from the log response ratio as \(100\times [{e}^{\beta }-1]\) and expressed as percentage changes in tree abundance associated with a 1 s.d. increase in each continuous predictor. Models were fitted for all plots across species–ecosections, separately for each ecoregion province, and for saplings and adult trees. The full models are provided in Extended Data Figs. 5 and 8.

Elevational shifts in stem abundance and basal area of species–ecosections were also modelled using glmmTMB with Gaussian error distribution and identity link. Predictors included the upper–lower difference in climate change, disturbance extent and their interactions (Extended Data Fig. 9). Species identity was included as a random effect. We also evaluated ecoregion province as an additional random intercept, but its variance was negligible and it had little influence on model results. Therefore, only species identity was retained in the final models.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 26 Nov 2026 17:13, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:24.

Aiming to continue an unbeaten streak and break into the top two of the League One table, Sheffield Wednesday will welcome Reading to Hillsborough on Saturday.

The hosts sit fourth and two points off second spot after a midweek draw, while their visitors have fallen to ninth spot following three straight defeats.

Sheffield Wednesday head back to Hillsborough on Saturday aiming to continue a positive start to life under Dave Challinor and close in on League One's automatic promotion spots.

He arrived to take over a side winless in four games after a strong start to their first season back in League One and with their sights set on a return to the Championship, as they lost their final two games under Henrik Pedersen and played out two draws under caretaker management.

The Owls were slow off the mark in cup action under the new boss, losing to Oldham Athletic and Accrington Stanley, but they would win his first two league games at the helm to return to the top six, beating Plymouth Argyle 3-0 and Barnsley 2-1 in an away South Yorkshire Derby thanks to Jamal Lowe's first-half brace.

A tough trip to Stevenage then followed on Tuesday, and the South Yorkshire outfit kept an unbeaten league run under Challinor in tact as the contest ended goalless, meaning they have scored five goals and conceded just one in his first three third-tier games at the helm.

Now sitting fourth and just two points behind third-placed Oxford United and second-placed Huddersfield Town, Sheffield Wednesday will aim to continue their positive run and return to winning ways at Hillsborough with a chance to break into the automatic promotion spots if other results go their way.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the trip to Yorkshire aiming to bounce back to form and move back within touching distance of the playoff places.

Reading made a positive start to their first full season under Leam Richardson, having also set their sights on challenging for a return to the Championship, earning 21 points from their first 12 games courtesy of six wins and just three defeats.

That culminated in consecutive wins over Leyton Orient and Barnsley, but the Royals have seen their form take a dip since, going on to draw away at Plymouth before suffering three straight league defeats heading into the weekend.

Broken up by a 5-0 FA Cup win over Peterborough United, Richardson's men lost 2-0 to Oxford United in League One and in an EFL Trophy penalty shootout to Bristol Rovers, before falling away at league leaders Stockport County and at home to strugglers Bromley last weekend as Victor Adeboyejo scored the only goal on the hour mark to earn Bromley just a third win of the term.

The dip in form has seen Reading drop to ninth spot and four points off the top six, and they will hope to arrest that slump and keep themselves in the top-six picture with a rebound victory in Saturday's tough test.

Sheffield Wednesday League One form:.

Sheffield Wednesday form (all competitions):.

Reading form (all competitions):.

Sheffield Wednesday will likely remain without Reece James, Max Lowe, Tyler Onyango and Mason Burstow on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Di'Shon Bernard and Liam Cooper have returned from injuries and will continue in a back three alongside Sil Swinkels, having kept two clean sheets in the last three games, as long as Cooper is declared fit after another slight concern.

Elsewhere, Jamal Lowe has lined up in a makeshift wing-back role in the absence of James and Lowe, but winger Jordi Liongola took that spot in midweek, while Louie Barry was fit to start at Stevenage after an injury layoff and could continue in support of front man Davis Keillor-Dunn.

Reading duo Paddy Lane and Benn Ward remain confined to the treatment room.

Jack Marriott will continue to lead the line, having netted nine goals in 11 league games this season, although Jamie Reid and Jacob Brown do also have claims for attacking spots, as does Kyreece Lisbie who was suspended last time out alongside Haydon Roberts.

Charlie Savage could also come back in from the outset, after George Earthy and Andy Rinomhota joined Lewis Wing in midfield last time out.

Sheffield Wednesday possible starting lineup:.

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels; Valery, Heskey, Bannan, J Lowe; Slattery, Keillor-Dunn, Barry.

Reading possible starting lineup:.

Pereira; Godwin-Malife, Knight, O'Connor, Roberts; Wing, Savage; Lisbie, Earthy, Brown; Marriott.

With two wins and a draw in League One since Challinor's appointment, Sheffield Wednesday appear to have rediscovered their groove and have been boosted by returns of several key men in recent weeks.

Taking on a Reading side hit by three straight defeats, we fancy the Owls to bounce back with another clean sheet and victory at Hillsborough at the weekend.

Zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. The Juventus full-back was named in Türkiye’s starting line-up for Sunday’s Nations League match against France. His left hamstring tightened up as he went through the warm-up. He was taken out of the matchday squad as a precaution. Barış Alper Yılmaz started in his place.

An Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead. Abdülkerim Bardakcı scored a late reply for Türkiye. The result left France top of Nations League Group A1 with 13 points. They are through to the quarter-finals, which are due next March.

According to recent reports, çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

According to recent reports, the location is what worries Juventus. Çelik was substituted at half-time in the 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes. His scans took place on the morning of Friday 23 October. He began a rehabilitation programme straight away and was expected back after the November break.

Tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

It has been revealed that çelik had only just returned after weeks out. That is why the warm-up incident has raised fears of a relapse. No diagnosis has yet been confirmed.

Juventus were already without Pierre Kalulu. He picked up the injury in the game against Fiorentina. He began treatment and was withdrawn from the France squad. Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

It has been revealed that if Çelik’s problem proves to be a relapse, Spalletti could be without both of his main right-sided defenders for those two games. The schedule offers little room for recovery. The Omonia match is the second of four games in 12 days.

Recent findings suggest that the league position adds pressure. After 11 rounds Juventus are seventh in Serie A with 18 points. Their record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats.

According to recent reports, venezia visit Turin first, at 12:30 on 22 November in round 12 of Serie A. Omonia then come to the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November in the Europa League league phase.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

According to recent reports, “The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we demonstrated in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

It was a chastening afternoon for the champions who last won at Welford Road in January 2023.

Phil Dowson, Saints’ director of rugby, felt his side were in the contest at the interval but bemoaned the fact that they were unable to handle Leicester’s second-half power surge.

It’s a major day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the latest campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Industry observers note that tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”.

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”.

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Manchester City are continuing to invest in young talent as they look to strengthen their squad for the future, with another exciting prospect emerging on their transfer radar.

Pep Guardiola’s side have reportedly moved into pole position for one of Borussia Dortmund’s most highly rated youngsters.

United States international Mathis Albert has attracted interest from several European clubs, but City are currently considered the favourites to secure his signature.

With the teenager’s first-team opportunities limited in Germany, the Premier League champions could look to take advantage of the situation.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester City are the frontrunners to sign Albert after making a formal approach during the summer transfer window.

In a recent development, the report claims City are prepared to offer the 17-year-old lucrative personal terms as they step up their pursuit. Their interest is serious, with the club previously prepared to meet a valuation in the region of €20 million (£16.7m).

Sources indicate that chelsea are also long-term admirers of the youngster and were reportedly willing to spend a similar amount last winter. Paris Saint-Germain previously made contact with Dortmund in 2025, while Arsenal and Liverpool have more recently been monitoring his situation.

However, City are currently viewed as being in the strongest position should Dortmund soften their stance.

Albert joined Borussia Dortmund from the LA Galaxy academy in 2024 and has quickly established himself as one of the most exciting young American talents in European football. He has already made Bundesliga appearances and earned senior international recognition with the United States.

In a recent development, despite his potential, opportunities under Niko Kovac have been limited this season. That lack of regular first-team football has encouraged several clubs to monitor his development, although Dortmund remain determined to keep hold of their young attacker.

The Bundesliga side have reportedly rejected approaches, including loan enquiries, and continue to view Albert as an notable part of their long-term prepares. They are also preparing a contract extension offer, with his current agreement running until June 2027.

There is another vital factor for City. Premier League regulations prevent English clubs from signing Albert permanently until he turns 18 in May, meaning any potential transfer would be geared towards next summer rather than an immediate move.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have been linked with a lot of players over the last few years.

Over £600 million has been spent on them and, more change is still needed.

Obviously, this isn't the outcome that the Anfield outfit will have wanted but, it's the hand that they've seemingly been dealt.

All of their rivals are constantly looking for ways to upgrade their team and, the more that they manage to do this, the better they become and the more difficult they are to beat.

Fans expected Liverpool to be competing for silverware this term but, now that feels like it all rests on their transfer prepares with the club now being handed a green light to sign one of their targets.

Barcelona want to sign Ayden Heaven which could give Liverpool the green light to sign Ronald Araujo.

One of the main positions that Liverpool needed to upgrade in the 2026-27 transfer window was their defence.

Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate both exited Anfield for free and, the performances of Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley were shoddy.

Throw in the fact that Bradley managed to suffer yet another long-term injury and, Liverpool were left with a bit-part defence.

That's why Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo were brought in.

Nobody knew how each defender would perform due to their lack of Premier League experience but, to the surprise of many, they've been two of the Reds' best players.

But, because Araujo is only on a season-long loan, his future is still undecided or, it was until this fresh patch from BBC Sport.

"Fulham and Barcelona are among the clubs to have expressed an interest in Heaven, with both having tried to sign him when he decided to leave Arsenal," they wrote.

"The England U20s defender's preference is believed to be a loan move, though he would also entertain permanent offers.

"At United he has largely been used as a back-up option and, after enjoying a run in the team under former manager Ruben Amorim, he lost his place under Michael Carrick. He returned to the side only after an injury crisis hit the club last season.

"Heaven is also capable of playing at left-back and in midfield, but does not expect to be trusted as a regular starter amid the instability at Old Trafford, with the club 19th in the league.

"He is under contract until 2029 in a deal that includes an option for an extra year.".

Ayden Heaven joining Barcelona could force Barcelona to sell Ronald Araujo.

Araujo's versatility is one of the best things about him.

The defender can be comfortably used as a centre-back or a right-back with Iraola using him in both positions this term.

Indeed, the Uruguayan's injury history is a bit of a worry but, touch wood, he's managed to keep fit while playing for Liverpool so far.

As mentioned, Araujo's future isn't set in stone yet but, if Barca manage to sign Heaven from Manchester United, it feels like Araujo would fall further down Hansi Flick's looks.

This could mean that the La Liga giants are willing to negotiate a cheaper deal for the centre-back which, judging by the recent developments from Liverpool, is exactly what they want.

Here's hoping that a deal can be reached soon and that Barcelona find a successor for their captain soon.

In a recent development, the reported £50million release clause provides some clarity over the financial side of a possible transfer. According to recent reports, A January move appears less realistic, with Galatasaray having little interest in losing a player they only signed in the summer. A deal next summer could be a more plausible scenario if Liverpool maintain their interest.

For now, the Reds’ reported scouting activity suggests Batrakov is firmly on their radar, but there is no indication that a formal bid has been submitted. Liverpool will need to continue monitoring his progress before deciding whether to pursue the £50million-rated midfielder.

By Joshua Cole | 26 Nov 2026 17:18.

Samsunspor will hope to record consecutive wins at Samsun Yeni 19 Mayis Stadium when they welcome Genclerbirligi on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts are 17th in the Turkish Super Lig standings with seven points from 11 matches, while the visitors occupy 12th place with 14 points from 12 games.

Since replacing Thorsten Fink in mid-October, Nenad Bjelica has managed just one win from five games, failing to deliver the immediate impact the Samsunspor hierarchy would have hoped for.

The Croatian's only win so far came at home against Konyaspor (1-0) in their penultimate game, ending a run of three defeats under him and eight for the club, although he can be forgiven for failing to build on that result.

The Red Lightning travelled to face champions and league leaders Galatasaray last time out and lost 2-1, a result Bjelica would not be too concerned about given the considerable gap in quality between the two sides.

However, the Samsun side will hope to get back on track against Genclerbirligi, a team they have not lost to since 2011 and one they beat 2-1 the last time both sides met at this ground last season.

Genclerbirligi will see this as the ideal opportunity to record another victory over Samsunspor, although their form on the road leaves plenty of questions.

The Youth have lost their last four away games, conceding 14 goals across those matches and failing to score, with their only away goal this season coming on their first trip to Goztepe, where they secured a 1-0 victory.

These challenges will leave Bernd Storck with concerns despite the consistency his team have shown in recent weeks, having recorded three wins in their last four games across all competitions.

Genclerbirligi secured a 1-0 home victory over Gaziantep in their last league game, having also recorded consecutive 5-0 victories over Alanyaspor in the league and Karakopru in the Turkish Cup, with the 3-0 away defeat to Besiktas being the only blemish in that run.

Emre Kilinc is a doubt, leaving Bjelica with a few selection decisions to make, although Mohamed Bayo is expected to lead the line again after scoring his first goal of the season against Galatasaray.

Genclerbirligi have several absentees, with Dimitrios Goutas ruled out for the season due to a cruciate ligament injury.

Kevin Rodrigues is also dealing with an injury, while Peter Etebo, Gokhan Akkan and Ensar Cavusoglu are doubts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V.

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

Jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had said he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

In between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

A man and a goal down, Chelsea then saw hundreds of their own fans walk out when Mathys Tel scored a brilliant second for Spurs with three minutes remaining. The visiting fans, who had seen one win at the Bridge since 1990 prior to Saturday, could hardly believe what they had seen.

Sources indicate that tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. The two benches had clashed and De Zerbi had been booked after Palmer’s first yellow card that the Italian felt should have been a red. But De Zerbi will not care about that now, with Tottenham’s season finally up and running thanks to successive league wins against Coventry City and Chelsea.

In a recent development, tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

With Solanke resting up on the bench until the 65th minute, De Zerbi moved Omar Marmoush, who had scored his first Spurs goal against Coventry, into the middle and brought in Tel on the left.

In a recent development, kinsky played a bad pass straight to Pedro Neto. The ball was worked to Henderson, but Kinsky recovered to make a save and then stopped the follow-up from Neto. The offside flag then went up, but it was unclear whether it would have spared Kinsky on both occasions had Chelsea scored.

It was not the first time Kinsky had handed possession back to Chelsea in a dangerous area, although the 23-year-old had also made a good save to palm away a curling effort from Palmer. That came after Fernandes had the ball pinched from him far too easily.

In a recent development, neto was Chelsea’s most dangerous player, but it was the wrong call by Alonso to leave Danny Welbeck on the bench, with João Pedro out injured, and he was too slow to change things. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Sources indicate that tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”.

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”.

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

In a recent development, but Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”.

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

Recent findings suggest that “We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”.

Amorim made four changes to the starting line-up from the team that beat Frosinone on Sunday. Two were enforced due to injuries, with Ardon Jashari replacing Luka Modric and Pervis Estupinan taking Davide Bartesaghi’s spot. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse and Omari Hutchinson came into the attack.

The first shot of the game took less than two minutes to come and it provided an example of the intense pressing that the home side have become known for, though Freuler’s effort from distance was a speculative one that sailed comfortably over.

Industry observers note that milan began to string some nice moves together, and they had a couple of attempts of their own from just beyond the edge of the box miss the target. The first came from Cisse, who cut inside and curled one well over and wide, then Jashari concluded a promising attack with a wild shot.

In a recent development, there were two moments of panic in quick succession for Milan. The first was when a cross from the right evaded everyone and fell to Martins, though thankfully his touch let him down in a dangerous area. Then, Goncalo Ramos had a rough fall and seemed to jar his knee, but he got up and played on with a grimace.

Sources indicate that the first shot on target fell to the home side and it came after Sankhoun Diawara lost possession inside his own half. Jota Silva picked up the ball and fed Pedersen, whose attempt was thankfully down the middle and caught by Mike Maignan.

Olympiacos continued to have the better of the scoring chances, as Martins began to find his range. Firstly he shot from distance but weakly and straight into Maignan’s arms, but then the Frenchman had to made a brilliant save at full-stretch to keep out the Portuguese’s strike.

Recent findings suggest that the trend of tame efforts from around 20 yards out continued midway through the first half up at the other end. Ramos won an aerial duel and collected it to try and gallop in behind, eventually laying it off for Moreira who didn’t really test Ortega.

Industry observers note that right on the half-hour mark, the home side took the lead. A corner kick from the left was defended awfully in truth, with Pirola getting the better of Diawara in a central area to head off the crossbar, off Maignan and in from six yards out. Going behind in the Europa League is by this point an all-too-familiar feeling.

Milan were inches away from getting themselves level rapidly as Pirola turned from the hero in one goalmouth to the hero at the other. A ball over the top found Cisse’s run in behind and Ortega came darting off his line but the ball squirmed through. The Italian somehow got a shot off from the floor that was rolling into the net but for Lirola’s last-ditch sliding clearance for a corner.

There was a flash point towards the end of the half which saw De Winter and Jota Silva both go into the box. A long ball over the top was eventually followed by play being blown dead for offside, yet the pair had a stand-up wrestling match for about 20 yards, until they both even ended up off the field.

Recent findings suggest that in the first of two minutes added on at the end of the half, Pirola had a chance to actually get his name on the scoresheet after the opener was labelled an own-goal. Some dire defending down the right ended with a cut-back that the former Inter youth academy man fired over from inside the box.

Recent findings suggest that amorim chose to make two changes at the break, as the American duo Christian Pulisic and Yunus Musah came on. Ramos and Estupinan were the ones to make way, with Cisse going up front and Moreira switching over to left wing-back.

Just as it looked like getting out of hand for Milan, Hutchinson scored a goal from nothing. Having seized possession inside his own half, the Englishman went on a brilliant solo run down the right where he was nearly clipped down twice, before jinking inside onto his preferred left foot and finding the bottom corner with a precise low shot.

Milan built on the goal that got them back into it, and six minutes later they drew themselves level. A sustained period of possession inside the Olympiacos half saw the ball worked nicely down the right side for Hutchinson to cross perfectly onto the head of Cisse at the far post, who headed in from a few yards out for his 10th of the campaign.

Industry observers note that as if things couldn’t get any more dramatic, Milan completed the comeback as they made it 3-2 with 20 minutes left on the clock. Hutchinson was again the man who did all of the hard work, getting the ball on the touchline and sitting his marker down before driving to the right edge of the box and standing up a cross for Pulisic. The substitute struck his volley perfectly, nestling it inside the post.

Milan made their final two changes either side of the third goal, with Filippo Terracciano replacing the cautioned Diawara, then Christian Comotto coming on for Cisse.

It was the Omari Hutchinson show in the second half, and the on-loan Nottingham Forest man should have had yet another assist when he darted past his man to fire in a low cross that squirmed to Moreira but was skewed wide.

With just a couple of minutes left there were huge penalty shouts from the Greek side after a header struck Tomori, though replays showed it hit his shoulder. The Rossoneri broke from that corner and had a four-on-one, however Hutchinson stumbled when playing the final pass, and Pulisic sent Moreira’s square pass into the stands.

The finale to the game saw Milan finally kill it off. Olympiacos had a corner that produced a scramble inside the box, which eventually saw Hutchinson emerge with it and lead another counter. He found Pulisic down the left who slid it across for Moreira on the right, and the former Strasbourg man settle it well, cut inside and fired into the bottom corner for the final act of a dramatic night.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he noted, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

The new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Sources indicate that before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

Recent findings suggest that the visit highlighted Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

Sources indicate that the financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

According to recent reports, the offer involves up to 208.5m upcoming shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment aims.

According to recent reports, the spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering latest players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

Manchester United transfer news: Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer, according to a report from The Athletic covered by CaughtOffside. The 32-year-old is unhappy with both the proposed salary and the length of the deal, and the standoff lands with his current contract set to expire in June 2027.

The calendar adds pressure. In 50 days, Fernandes can open talks with foreign clubs, and Galatasaray have already been linked. United hold a 12-month extension option that stops him leaving for free, but triggering it only postpones the argument and keeps an unhappy captain in the dressing room.

The refusal follows a bad few weeks. After a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics, and Carrick dropped him for the Bournemouth game. Carrick has since been sacked with United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, so Mauricio Pochettino inherits the standoff alongside a team in trouble.

His strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

In a recent development, pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

United should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

Sources indicate that the sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

It has been revealed that if Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

James Penrice has warned that Rangers can forget about going top of the table on Saturday if they play like they did for the first 45 minutes against Aberdeen.

Derek McInnes’ side were a goal down at half-time and heading to their first defeat in 14 games after failing to get going against the Dons.

James Penrice has warned Rangers they will need to improve if they are to take top spot.

Rangers goalscorers Djeidi Gassama, Nico Raskin and Ryan Naderi celebrate against Aberdeen.

‘We could have done that and made it easy for ourselves.’.

‘It wasn’t ideal, but he was still happy afterward because we won the game.

By Joshua Cole | 26 Nov 2026 17:18.

Gaziantep will be looking to halt their alarming slide when they welcome Amed SK to Gaziantep Stadium on Saturday, with the visitors also aiming to end a run of defeats.

The Falcons are 16th in the Turkish Super Lig table with eight points from 11 matches and find themselves in the relegation zone, while the visitors sit fourth on 23 points, having made an impressive start to life in the top flight.

Volkan Demirel started his tenure with defeat, losing 1-0 at Genclerbirligi, failing to make an immediate impact after replacing Orhan Ak, who won just two of Gaziantep's opening 11 matches.

The Falcons had lost six matches consecutively before Demirel took charge and are now on a seven-game losing streak, with only Eyupspor (nine games) having a longer run of defeats.

Before their recent loss, Gaziantep suffered defeats against Kasimpasa, Trabzonspor, Erzurumspor, Istanbul Basaksehir, Corum and Kocaelispor, conceding 15 goals across their losing streak.

Their defensive problems have been particularly concerning, but their attack has equally struggled, with the Falcons scoring just twice across their last eight games, a period in which they have collected only one point while failing to find the net in six of those matches.

In what will be the first-ever meeting between the two sides, Amed SK will hope to respond after losing at home for the first time this season in their last league game, with Caykur Rizespor leaving Diyarbakir Stadium with a 2-0 win.

It was the first time the Talaytepe side had dropped points at home this season and followed a 4-3 defeat at Galatasaray, making it their first consecutive losses of the campaign.

Generally, Besnik Hasi's side have enjoyed a productive campaign and established themselves among the leading teams in the Super Lig, but they are now looking to avoid a run of three consecutive matches without a point, although their away form leaves some room for pessimism.

Amed have won just one of their five away games this season, losing two and drawing two, while they have conceded in every single away match, letting in at least two goals in four of those five outings.

Chelsea Transfer News: Alonso Tells Right-Back To Leave

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso has reportedly told Malo Gusto to find a fresh club, according to CaughtOffside, who are citing Simon Phillips’ Substack.
  • They tried to sign Gusto on loan on deadline day, but Chelsea refused anything short of a permanent deal.
  • Recent findings suggest that gusto’s standing has slipped quickly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso has reportedly told Malo Gusto to find a fresh club, according to CaughtOffside, who are citing Simon Phillips’ Substack. The report claims the 23-year-old France international does not suit the wing-back system Alonso has built at Stamford Bridge. It also floats a surprise swap that would send Gusto to Liverpool and reunite Alonso with Jeremie Frimpong, his former Bayer Leverkusen right wing-back.

Liverpool’s interest has history. They tried to sign Gusto on loan on deadline day, but Chelsea refused anything short of a permanent deal. Their right-back problem has run since Trent Alexander-Arnold left. Frimpong cost around £29.5million and has battled injuries and form, while Ronald Araujo is a centre-back covering on a season-long loan from Barcelona.

Recent findings suggest that gusto’s standing has slipped quickly. He started three of the first four league games, yet Josh Acheampong has since taken his place, and reports say he will be fourth choice behind Acheampong, Marco Palestra and Reece James once James returns from injury in early 2027.

Recent findings suggest that his strength is defending, with 73 tackles and 36 chances created in 45 appearances last season. The weakness is end product, because three goals and five assists are modest for a wing-back who must supply Alonso’s right-hand width.

Sources indicate that frimpong supplies exactly that. The 25-year-old Dutchman scored 28 of his 30 Leverkusen goals under Alonso and thrives on pace and early crosses. Defending is his flaw, at 5ft 8in and with a poor injury record at Anfield.

No. Chelsea are fifth with 16 points from 10 games, but they have lost four, including 1-0 at Sunderland last Sunday and 3-0 at Brentford, and they concede too easily. Frimpong would add another attacker to a right side that already has James, Acheampong, Palestra and Pedro Neto, and he does nothing for a shaky back line. With no European football this season, Chelsea don’t need that many right-sided options anyway.

The money matters too. Both players have contracts until 2030 and similar valuations, so a straight swap brings Chelsea no cash and leaves Liverpool with their problem solved.

Recent findings suggest that sell Gusto instead, preferably abroad, since Paris Saint-Germain have been linked and Chelsea are reportedly open to cutting their asking price. Then spend that fee on a defensive midfielder or centre-back, because that is where Alonso’s team needs help.

#129085. An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals

An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 120 min read (24040 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~120 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2.
  • The bulk of crop production worldwide strictly depends on rainfall to support irrigation needs, and limitations on water availability pose a global challenge for agricultural productivity, with water scarcity and drought stress incurring unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects on yield1,2.
  • It has been revealed that conventional plant-breeding efforts have boosted crop yields in water-limited environments, for example, through improved stress resistance, greater biomass accumulation, delayed leaf senescence or ‘stay-green’ strategies7,10, but broad potential remains for improving yield and yield stability across growing regions regardless of water availability11,12.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30–40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4–32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7–42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

The bulk of crop production worldwide strictly depends on rainfall to support irrigation needs, and limitations on water availability pose a global challenge for agricultural productivity, with water scarcity and drought stress incurring unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects on yield1,2. The adverse effects of climate change on crop productivity have historically been underestimated5. With the average global temperature expected to increase by 1.5–2.0 °C by 2050, the frequency and severity of drought events will be further increased, which could be accompanied by 30–40% reductions in food production3,4. Despite facing the greatest food-security challenges in the modern era7,8, annual crop yield improvement rates have not kept pace with projected food demands, that is, a 50–70% increase to accommodate approximately 9.8 billion people worldwide by 2050 (ref. 9), further compounding the effects of disaster events and decreasing availability of arable land.

It has been revealed that conventional plant-breeding efforts have boosted crop yields in water-limited environments, for example, through improved stress resistance, greater biomass accumulation, delayed leaf senescence or ‘stay-green’ strategies7,10, but broad potential remains for improving yield and yield stability across growing regions regardless of water availability11,12. Increasingly precise genetic modification strategies have advanced crop engineering for drought resistance13,14,15,16,17. For example, heterologous expression of a rice trehalose-6-phosphate phosphatase in developing maize ears improves yield under both well-watered and drought-stress conditions in the field16. In cassava, expressing a modified Arabidopsis potassium (K+) channel in vascular tissues improves K+ transport, photosynthesis and root biomass, allowing enhanced productivity in nutrient-poor and drought-prone environments17. However, genetic modification usually cannot provide a single, universal solution to multifactorial drought stress, and this approach frequently fails to improve yields in the field13,18 because drought resistance is a complex quantitative trait involving a multitude of small-effect loci or genes mediating diverse stress responses, such as stomatal closure (for reduced transpiration) or modified root architecture (for enhanced water uptake)10,19. Drought resistance typically accompanies trade-offs by way of reduced yield in the absence of stress6,20, undermining the effectiveness of certain genetic modification strategies. Therefore, of the genes identified in controlled conditions that often show limited effects in real-world environments, relatively few undergo rigorous field trials to properly demonstrate consistent agronomic value21.

In a recent development, among known genetic resources for drought resistance, lichens have been generally overlooked despite their ubiquitous distribution across extreme ecological niches. In arid-adapted lichens, mycobionts appear to contribute more to survival under water deficit than photobionts22,23. We have previously isolated the lichen-forming fungus Endocarpon pusillum, which has extreme drought resistance. Exposure to dehydration stress identified 1,781 differentially expressed E. pusillum genes24. Through mining those data, here we identified the transcription factor gene EpTFIIAγ that broadly enhances yield and biomass production under field conditions when heterologously expressed in the world’s top-three-produced staple cereal crops of bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), maize (Zea mays L.) and rice (Oryza sativa L.). EpTFIIAγ delays plant senescence, enhances photosynthetic capacity, water-use efficiency (WUE) and drought resistance by functioning as a transcriptional co-factor to coordinately target multiple genes and pathways. EpTFIIAγ binds to TATA-box-containing motifs and interacts with several endogenous wheat transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance networks involved in stress responses, plant development, photosynthesis and grain yield. Our results provide an unprecedented broad-spectrum resource for crop improvement and highlight the untapped potential of lichen mycobionts as sources of versatile transgenes for biotechnology.

Industry observers note that among 25 differentially expressed genes predicted to encode transcription factors identified under dehydration stress in E. pusillum (Fig. 1a), EPUS02736 exhibits the strongest upregulation and encodes a transcription initiation factor IIA γ-chain (designated EpTFIIAγ). EpTFIIAγ shares homology with TFIIAs from plants, such as Arabidopsis, wheat, rice and maize, although the genetic relatedness between EpTFIIAγ and these homologues is relatively distant (Fig. 1b). Strong expression under dehydration stress implicates EpTFIIAγ in drought adaptation of the lichen mycobiont. Towards understanding its functionality, EpTFIIAγ was expressed in the yeast ∆hog1 mutant (deficient in HOG1, which encodes the high osmolarity glycerol 1 protein kinase), resulting in remarkably enhanced growth on solid synthetic dropout (SD) −Ura medium with 0.75 M sorbitol (Fig. 1c), and statistically significantly higher growth in corresponding liquid medium than the control (Fig. 1d). These results suggested that EpTFIIAγ contributes to regulating osmotic stress.
